title: Disentangling Local and Global Semantics in Diffusion Models for Image Editing
authors: Plitsis M.; Kouzelis T.; Koromilas P.; Katsouros V.; A. Nicolaou M.; Panagakis Y.
abstract: Diffusion models have achieved state-of-the-art image synthesis, yet unlike GANs, they lack a well-structured latent space for intuitive image editing. Existing diffusion-based editing methods often rely on supervised fine-tuning or text-based guidance, while recent unsupervised techniques leveraging the model’s bottleneck layer suffer from one or more key limitations: (i) they focus only on global attributes, (ii) fail to disentangle local and global semantics, or (iii) require extensive human intervention. To fill this gap, we first propose an unsupervised method for localized image editing in pre-trained unconditional diffusion models that disentangles local and global semantics in the model’s latent space. Given an input image and a user-specified region of interest, our approach uses the denoising network’s Jacobian to map that region to a corresponding latent subspace. We then separate this subspace into shared (global) and region-specific components to uncover latent directions that control local attributes. These directions generalize across images, enabling semantically consistent edits without retraining. We go one step further by extending our method to minimize manual supervision by automatically inferring edit directions from a single reference image and generating region masks without human input. Experiments on multiple datasets show that our method yields more localized, high-fidelity edits than state-of-the-art approaches. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Comparative Evaluation of TTS and Vocoder Architectures in Lip-to-Speech Synthesis
authors: Wakizaka S.; Zhang H.; Saitoh T.
abstract: This paper presents a comparative evaluation of model architectures in Lip-to-Speech (L2S) synthesis, a technique that reconstructs speech waveforms directly from lip motion videos. Building on the Lip2Wav framework, we examine the impact of different model components on the quality of generated speech. Specifically, we evaluate four model configurations by combining two types of Text-to-Speech (TTS) models—Tacotron2 and FastSpeech2—with two types of speech synthesis models—Griffin-Lim and HiFi-GAN. Experiments were conducted on both English and Japanese datasets, and the resulting synthesized speech was evaluated using multiple objective metrics, including STOI, ESTOI, and PESQ, to assess intelligibility and perceptual quality. Results show that the Tacotron2 + Griffin-Lim configuration achieved the highest scores in terms of intelligibility and naturalness, while the FastSpeech2 + HiFi-GAN configuration demonstrated superior acoustic fidelity and subjective quality. Furthermore, pretraining on Japanese datasets led to improved performance on English test data, indicating a positive effect of cross-lingual transfer. © 2026 SPIE.

title: TransGAN-WT: A Transformer-GAN Hybrid Model for Anomaly Detection in Wind Turbine SCADA Multivariate Time Series
authors: Kang J.
abstract: Wind turbine Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems generate large-scale multivariate time-series data that are essential for condition monitoring and predictive maintenance. However, reliable anomaly detection remains challenging because highly correlated operating sequences introduce substantial temporal redundancy, while subtle anomalies often produce reconstruction errors that overlap with normal operational fluctuations. To address these limitations, this paper proposes TransGAN-WT, a Transformer-Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) hybrid framework for unsupervised anomaly detection in wind turbine SCADA data. The framework is designed to address two key problems: redundant temporal representations and insufficient separation between normal and subtle anomalous patterns. A cross-scale temporal interaction mechanism captures complementary dependencies at different temporal resolutions, while a two-stage autoregressive reconstruction strategy progressively enhances the reconstruction-error separation associated with subtle anomalies. Adversarial learning is further integrated with Transformer-based reconstruction to improve representation discrimination under complex operating conditions. Experiments on twelve real-world wind turbine SCADA datasets show that TransGAN-WT achieves an average F1-score of 96.10% and a false positive rate of 0.06%, outperforming the evaluated baseline methods. Repeated-run analysis yields an average F1-score of 95.0% with a standard deviation of 0.008, indicating stable performance across independent runs. Component-wise ablation experiments further quantify the individual contributions of the cross-scale interaction, autoregressive reconstruction, and adversarial learning mechanisms, while sensitivity analysis evaluates the influence of the temporal window configuration. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed framework for unsupervised anomaly detection in complex wind turbine operating environments.  © 2013 IEEE.

title: FTS-GAN: A novel fuzzy-driven GAN model for sparse data handling and robust temporal modeling
authors: Jahani A.; Mehrabi A.; Khalilpour S.A.; Seyedi H.; Nikoofard A.; Taghirad H.D.
abstract: Despite extensive efforts in time series imputation, data sparsity remains a significant challenge. In recent years, the emergence of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has partially addressed this issue. GAN models introduce noise and complexity, resulting in the generation of data that diverges from the inherent patterns of real-world time series. Consequently, this can negatively impact the performance of machine learning models. In this study, we propose a new approach that enhances the robustness of GANs by incorporating fuzzification as a powerful preprocessing step for denoising and extracting the underlying structure of time series data. The proposed framework consists of two main components, fuzzification and the GAN model. The essential characteristics of the time series are extracted through fuzzification and then fed into the discriminator network. The performance of the proposed method is assessed using Bi-LSTM and LightGBM on the M5 Competition, Air Quality, and Food Chain Store datasets. On M5 Competition, using 90 day windows and training on samples with fewer than 10 missing values while discarding windows with more than 40 missing values, fuzzification yields an RMSE reduction of up to 36%. On Air Quality, with 15% random masking and a missing value threshold of 5, it improves RMSEnonzero by up to 15%. On the Food Chain Store dataset, removing series with more than 16 missing values and training with at most 10 missing values, it reduces mean RMSE by up to 33%. Experimental results indicate that fuzzification improves the quality of GAN generated data and reinforces the overall advantage of the proposed framework. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Geology-Constrained Time Series Generative Adversarial Network for Well Log Curve Reconstruction
authors: Guo H.; Liao W.; Zhao B.; Cheng X.; Wang K.
abstract: The anomalous logging responses caused by complex geological and downhole engineering conditions, which can be the expansion of a borehole, the formation of fractures, and the mud intrusion, usually result in the absence of some important curves and undermine the accuracy of the reservoir evaluation. The strong nonlinearity and non-stationarity of the log curves remain problematic to conventional interpolation and statistical techniques; the traditional models do not take into account any sequential relationship between points along the depth axis, whereas the deep sequence models can only regress on the points, which limits their capability of ensuring the overall geological consistency. In order to resolve these difficulties, this paper introduces a Geology-Balanced Time Series Conditional Generative Adversarial Network (GC-TSGAN) in which the lithological data is converted into an initial state in the form of prior conditions and is input into both the generator and the discriminator. The model uses LSTM to learn depth-sequential dependencies and a BCE GAN-based adversarial loss to achieve distributional consistency and local morphological fidelity. Hyperparameter tuning is used with the help of random search and Bayesian optimization. The logging data of 41 wells in the B Basin, Chad, are experimented using GC-TSGAN alongside baseline models such as RF, XGBoost, LSTM and ANN; GC-TSGAN is proven to be much better than baseline models in terms of the RMSE, MAE, and squares of predicate and value. The findings confirm that the proposed model can effectively reconstruct log curves with high precision even in a complicated geological environment, thereby providing quality data for performing geological modeling and evaluating the reservoirs. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Feature-consistent cyclic domain adversarial network for unsupervised transfer diagnosis of the autoimmune disease IgG4-RD by Raman spectroscopy
authors: Zhang Z.; Chen C.; Qin W.; Wu X.; Liu Y.; Wu L.; Lv X.; Chang C.; Chen X.; Chen Z.; Xu Q.; Li Z.; Ma M.; Chen C.
abstract: IgG4-related disease (IgG4-RD) is a rare multi-organ immune disease with a complex pathogenesis and systemic clinical manifestations, which poses tremendous challenges for clinical diagnosis. Conventional diagnostic models based on supervised machine learning or deep learning are severely limited by the scarcity of labeled data arising from the above clinical characteristics of the disease. To address this problem, we propose a Feature-Consistent Cyclic Domain Adversarial Network (FCCDAN) framework specially designed for the one-dimensional time-series characteristics of Raman spectral data and the demand for scarce labeled data in IgG4-RD diagnosis. This framework innovatively designs a 1D Patch-GAN discriminator and introduces bidirectional feature consistency loss on both the generator and the discriminator to construct a pixel-semantic-feature three-level cross-domain alignment system. By taking common autoimmune diseases as the knowledge source, FCCDAN achieves high-performance unsupervised transfer diagnosis for IgG4-RD and demonstrates its excellent generalization ability on datasets of homologous autoimmune diseases and non-homologous diseases, with an average diagnostic accuracy of up to 90.62%—4.36% higher than that of the best baseline model. In addition, we combine Grad-CAM visualization with the pathological mechanism analysis of Raman spectra to highlight the key spectral features that influence model decision-making and explore potential molecular biomarkers of IgG4-RD and related autoimmune diseases, thus greatly enhancing the interpretability and clinical credibility of the model. FCCDAN is the first to integrate cyclic adversarial unsupervised domain adaptation technology with Raman spectroscopy for the diagnosis of autoimmune diseases, making up for the deficiency that existing diagnostic methods based on Raman spectroscopy generally lack cross-domain generalization ability. This effectively expands the application scope of Raman spectroscopy in label-scarce diagnostic scenarios while maintaining high performance and interpretability, and provides a valuable and feasible framework for the intelligent diagnosis of similar rare diseases with scarce labeled data in clinical practice. © 2026

title: Bayesian Generative Adversarial Networks via Gaussian Approximation for Tabular Data Synthesis
authors: Nasution B.I.; Elliot M.; Allmendinger R.
abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) has been used in many studies to synthesise mixed tabular data. Conditional tabular GAN (CTGAN) has been the most popular variant but struggle to effectively navigate the risk-utility trade-off. Bayesian GAN has received less attention for tabular data, but have been explored with unstructured data such as images and text. The most used technique employed in Bayesian GAN is Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC), but it is computationally intensive, particularly in terms of weight storage. In this paper, we introduce Gaussian Approximation of CTGAN (GACTGAN), an integration of the Bayesian posterior approximation technique using Stochastic Weight Averaging-Gaussian (SWAG) within the CTGAN generator to synthesise tabular data. Our results show that GACTGAN frequently improves tabular structure preservation and inferential utility, while maintaining comparable or lower disclosure risk in several datasets. These results highlight GACTGAN as a simpler, effective implementation of Bayesian tabular synthesis. © 2026 University of Skovde. All rights reserved.

title: Long-horizon building energy control with Mamba forecasting, rectified flow scenarios, and synthetic data bridging
authors: Mirzamohammadi M.; Varzeghani N.M.; Navazani M.
abstract: Buildings account for approximately 30–40% of global final energy consumption and nearly one-third of greenhouse gas emissions, making intelligent energy management a critical pathway toward decarbonization. Model predictive control (MPC) has emerged as a powerful framework for building energy management due to its ability to optimize energy cost, thermal comfort, and operational constraints under uncertainty. However, the effectiveness of MPC is highly dependent on the quality and temporal consistency of load and temperature forecasts, while access to sufficient real building data is often limited by privacy and availability constraints. This paper proposes an integrated building energy management framework that combines multi-scale synthetic data generation, a modern state-space sequence forecaster, and MPC. A multi-scale hierarchical generative adversarial network (MS-HGAN) is employed to generate privacy-preserving synthetic trajectories that augment limited real training data for forecasting, rather than acting as a control surrogate. Forecasting is performed using a Mamba-based state-space model with a Random Forest (RF-Tree) output regressor, and the resulting predictions are embedded into an MPC architecture with probabilistic constraints and a safety filter. The proposed approach is evaluated on a large commercial multi-zone shopping mall (retail center) operating in a temperate climate region (Tehran-like, Köppen Csa). To support augmentation under privacy constraints, MS-HGAN is trained on auxiliary building energy time-series datasets and is used to enrich the training distribution of the forecaster via a controlled real-only, synthetic-only, and mixed real–synthetic study. Comprehensive evaluations are conducted using both short-term (30-day) and long-term (one-year) closed-loop simulations. Results show that mixed real–synthetic training improves forecasting robustness and translates into superior MPC performance in terms of energy savings, reduced comfort violations, and peak-load shaving, compared with deterministic MPC and strong learning-based baselines, including LSTM/GRU, ARX, S4, and diffusion-based predictors. The findings provide direct evidence that privacy-motivated synthetic augmentation can play a complementary and measurable role in improving predictive control performance for commercial buildings through the forecasting-to-MPC pathway. © The Author(s) 2026.

title: Image Inpainting in 30 Years: A Survey
authors: Yu Z.; Zhao H.; Zhang W.; Song W.; Zheng Y.; Nappi M.; Chen J.
abstract: As a fundamental task in restoring continuous visual signals, image inpainting plays a critical role in autonomous driving perception, medical imaging, video editing and digital heritage preservation. Driven by deep learning and large-scale generative models, the field has transitioned from low-level texture synthesis to high-level semantic generation, yielding major breakthroughs in structural fidelity and visual realism. Centring on the generative paradigm as the architectural trajectory, this survey systematically categorizes the 30-year evolution of image inpainting into three distinct technological generations: traditional prior-driven synthesis, deep learning data-driven reconstruction and modern foundation model-driven generation. Despite this progress, highly competitive methods still struggle with large-scale missing regions, global consistency in complex scenes, fine-grained micro-details and alignment with human visual perception. To address these gaps, we critically evaluate the technical paradigms and main bottlenecks within each of these evolutionary stages. We categorize and compare mainstream breakthroughs across high-resolution restoration, text-guided synthesis and complex scene generation. Furthermore, we compile standard benchmarks, evaluation metrics and quantitative performance comparisons of representative algorithms. Finally, we dissect open challenges—focusing on cross-scene generalization and evaluation metric alignment—and outline future trajectories, particularly the integration of inpainting with text-guided foundation models, providing a definitive reference for future theoretical and engineering advancements. © 2026 John Wiley & Sons Ltd.

title: Research on the Expansion Methodology of Encrypted Traffic Data in the Industrial Internet Based on Conditional VAE-GAN
authors: Wang Y.; Wang G.; Gao Y.; Huo C.
abstract: With the rapid development of the industrial Internet, network security has become one of the key factors restricting the healthy development of the industrial Internet. Traffic classification and anomaly detection are important means in the network security protection system, and the implementation of the above research is inseparable from the support of high-quality datasets. However, at present, due to problems such as enterprise privacy and data collection, there are few public industrial Internet traffic datasets. To solve this problem, this paper proposes a method for industrial Internet traffic data augmentation, Conditional VAE-GAN (Conditional variational autoencoder generative adversarial network). By integrating the advantages of VAE (Variational Autoencoder) and GAN (Generative Adversarial Network) in data augmentation, the model embeds self-attention and channel attention mechanisms in the convolutional layer structure of encoder and decoder to improve the model representation ability, and combines BiLSTM (Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory) to enhance the model's extraction of traffic time series features, to generate high-quality traffic data with time series correlation and feature diversity. To verify the quality of the generated dataset, this paper uses SCRNN (Time Series Convolutional Recurrent Neural Network) as the traffic classifier and compares this data generation method with traditional sampling techniques and diffusion models. Experiments show that the classification accuracy, precision, recall and F1-Score of the dataset generated in this paper are improved by 17%, 10%, 15% and 14%, respectively, compared with the original few-sample dataset.  © 2025 Copyright held by the owner/author(s).

title: AI-Driven Image Generation: Algorithms, Architectures, Quality Assessment, and Applications—A Structured Narrative Review
authors: Leszczuk M.; Zhang Y.; Farias M.C.Q.; Chandler D.M.; Kalola R.
abstract: Background: This paper presents a structured narrative review of recent advances in AI-driven image generation across four complementary perspectives: generative models and architectures, quality assessment and performance metrics, application domains, and multi-modal or cross-lingual extensions. The review aimed to identify dominant methodological trends, representative evaluation practices, and open research challenges in contemporary image generation research. Methods: A structured literature search was conducted in the Scopus database on 29 January 2026 using a predefined query focused on modern generative-image paradigms and excluding clearly out-of-scope domains. Eligible records addressed contemporary AI-driven image generation or closely related multi-modal generation settings within the temporal and topical scope of the search. Retrieved records were first assigned to four thematic branches and then screened with branch-specific relevance criteria for narrative synthesis. Results: The search returned 1524 records, and the final narrative synthesis included 117 publications: 34 on generative models, 23 on quality assessment, 29 on applications, and 31 on multi-modal and cross-lingual aspects. Across the reviewed literature, progress was shaped not only by visual fidelity, but also by controllability, semantic grounding, human-centred evaluation, multi-modal integration, and practical deployment constraints. Limitations: The review was limited to a single primary bibliographic source and to a qualitative narrative synthesis without meta-analysis. Conclusions: The review provides a structured reference point for researchers and practitioners working on AI-based image generation and its evaluation, while also highlighting benchmark, comparability, and multi-modal-transfer challenges that remain unresolved. © 2026 by the authors.

title: Attention-enhanced wasserstein GAN for agricultural market data imputation

title: NCPLS-ViT: Enhancing Vision transformer with nested patch scheduling for cervical cancer classification through contrastive Self-Supervised learning
authors: Lavanya Devi N.; Aravind Britto K.R.; Savithri C.N.; Anu Jemila G.R.
abstract: Cervical cancer continues to pose a major global health concern, emphasizing the need for an accurate and early diagnostic classification system. Whole Slide Image (WSI) classification has emerged as a promising automated alternative to traditional manual screening. However, deep learning models face challenges due to high inter/intra-class variability, class imbalance, and complex tissue morphology. To overcome these issues, this research proposes a self-supervised-based deep learning approach using the Nested Convolutional Patch Layer Scheduling-based Vision Transformer (NCPLS-ViT) model for WSI-based cervical histopathology image classification. Unlike existing approaches that rely on conventional patch-based classification, NCPLS-ViT introduces a hierarchical patch extraction module, employing nested convolutional patch extraction and spatial shifting to effectively capture multi-scale tissue structures while preserving spatial relationships. Additionally, a self-supervised instance representation learning module leverages contrastive self-supervised learning (CSSL) to improve feature discrimination across both labeled and unlabeled data, ensuring more robust feature embeddings. An adaptive patch scheduling module is proposed to maximize information processing by introducing a self-attention-based ranking mechanism that allows the model to pay attention to diagnostically important areas with less redundancy. Moreover, the WSI decision classification module driven by a Transformer-based classification head leverages the capability of patch-level to aggregate into a final whole-slide prediction that outperforms the constraints of CNN-based aggregation strategies. In the solution to the critical problem of imbalance in classes, the model applies Multi-Attention Generative Adversarial Network (MAGAN), which generates synthetic patches of underrepresented classes, which greatly improves the generalization. title: MAML-based temporal supervised information maximizing GAN for few-shot time series data generation

title: Efficient, Robust, and Anti-Collusion Fingerprinting of Image Diffusion Models
authors: Fei J.; Dai Y.; Xia Z.; Cao X.; Zhou J.; Piva A.; Tondi B.
abstract: Model fingerprinting, embedding user-specific identifiers (fingerprints) into generated outputs, has recently emerged as a popular solution to protect the intellectual property rights (IPR) of generative text-to-image (T2I) models and prevent unauthorized redistribution. In this work, we reveal a previously unexplored systematic vulnerability in existing generative model fingerprinting methods: they lack robustness against collusion attacks, where multiple attackers combine their models to remove or obscure the fingerprints. To address this issue, we take the first step towards a robust fingerprinting method for T2I models with anti-collusion capabilities. The proposed method encodes strings of bits, namely fingerprints, into the coefficients of a personalized normalization module (PNM) incorporated into T2I models, so that fingerprints can be reliably recovered from any generated image. To defend against collusion attacks and prevent unauthorized model redistribution, we introduce an anti-collusion mechanism based on lossless function-invariant parameter transformations. This mechanism significantly degrades the image generation quality of colluded models, making them effectively unusable. Moreover, our method allows developers to efficiently create multiple copies of fingerprinted T2I models by reparameterizing the PNM without the need for retraining. We also introduce a worst-case optimization strategy to improve robustness against model-level attacks. Our experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves high fidelity and robustness across multiple T2I image generation and editing tasks, with fingerprint extraction accuracy exceeding 99.5%. Compared with existing methods, our method demonstrates, for the first time, a notable proactive robustness to collusion attack by significantly increasing the FID of colluded models.  © 1979-2012 IEEE.

title: Discriminating Market Anomalies Using Partitioned Local Depth: A Time Series Analysis of Flash Crashes and Structured Financial Events

title: Detecting violent deepfakes: dataset and a compact attention network with multi-scale supervision

title: Synthetic image detection with CLIP: Understanding and assessing predictive cues

title: Synthetic data generation methods for longitudinal and time series health data: a systematic review
authors: Miletic M.; Sariyar M.
abstract: Background: Synthetic data generation (SDG) has emerged as a critical enabler for data-driven healthcare research, offering privacy-preserving alternatives to real patient data. Temporal health data – ranging from physiological signals to electronic health records (EHRs) – pose unique challenges for SDG due to their complexity, irregularity, and clinical sensitivity. Objective: This review systematically examines SDG methods for longitudinal and time-series health data. Its aims are to (1) propose a lightweight taxonomy to support orientation across the SDG landscape along five structural dimensions, (2) characterize the major synthesis techniques and their alignment with temporal structures and data modalities, and (3) synthesize the utility and privacy evaluation strategies used in practice. Methods: A systematic literature review was conducted following PRISMA guidelines across four major databases (ACM, arXiv, IEEE Xplore, Europe PMC) for publications from 2017 to 2025. Eligible studies proposed or applied SDG techniques to healthcare-relevant temporal data with sufficient methodological transparency. Structured data extraction and thematic analysis were used to identify modeling trends, evaluation metrics, and domain-specific requirements, complemented by a comparative synthesis of SDG methods. Results: A total of 115 studies were included. Deep generative models – especially Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Autoencoders (AEs), and diffusion-based methods – dominate the field, with increasing adoption of autoregressive and hybrid simulation approaches. Event-based EHR data are most commonly targeted, while continuous and irregular time series remain underexplored. Utility evaluations vary widely, with strong emphasis on descriptive statistics and predictive performance, but limited attention to inferential validity and clinical realism. Privacy assessments are sparse and inconsistently reported: only 30% of studies included any metric, and just around 6% implemented differential privacy (DP), often without parameter disclosure. This limited adoption may reflect technical challenges, limited expertise, and the absence of regulatory incentives. However, SDG research remains fragmented in terminology, evaluation practices, and privacy safeguards. Responsible-AI considerations – such as fairness, transparency, and trust – along with evidence on clinical adoption remain underexplored but are critical for future integration. This review provides a unified conceptual and methodological framework to guide future research, standardization efforts, and interdisciplinary collaboration for responsible, effective use of synthetic health data. © The Author(s) 2025.

title: Reconstruction-Based Methods for Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection: A Review and Taxonomy

Classical statistical, machine learning, deep learning, and generative approaches have all been applied to forecasting tasks in these fields, but comparisons between them are usually confined to a single domain or to models from the same family, and few studies report both univariate and multivariate results under the same conditions. This paper presents a controlled cross-domain comparison of four representative paradigms: classical statistics (Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average with Exogenous variables, SARIMAX), gradient boosting machine learning (Light Gradient Boosting Machine, LightGBM), recurrent deep learning (Recurrent Neural Network, RNN), and generative-adversarial deep learning (Conditional Generative Adversarial Network, CGAN). Each model is evaluated on three monthly datasets with contrasting characteristics: Bitcoin prices (175 observations, high volatility), U.S. energy consumption (612 observations, strong seasonality), and U.S. cardiovascular mortality (300 observations, gradual trend with pandemic shock). Both univariate and multivariate variants are tested under the same preprocessing and one-step-ahead evaluation protocols, using eight performance metrics. The CGAN reaches the lowest MAPE on energy consumption (2.88%). On Bitcoin, the multivariate LightGBM lowers the MAPE from 28.26 to 19.25%, while on cardiovascular mortality the RNN reaches 3.34% MAPE. title: Chillers fault identification using volunteered minority oversampling via OC-SVM with bounding and minimizing loss
authors: Prabhu Bam R.V.; Prabhu Gaonkar R.S.; Pazhayidam George C.
abstract: Class imbalance poses a major challenge in fault detection for Heating, Ventilation, and Air Conditioning (HVAC) systems, as limited fault data skews models and hampers the recognition of minority fault types. To address this, we introduce a Volunteered Minority Sample Generation (VMSG) method that produces balanced datasets for reliable fault classification. VMSG uses One-Class Support Vector Machine (OC-SVM) to learn the system’s normal behavior from abundant fault-free data. By measuring distances from the OC-SVM hyperplane, VMSG identifies minority fault instances that best characterize specific fault conditions as “volunteers”. These volunteers then help generate synthetic samples to enrich the training set and address class imbalance. Typically, conventional OC-SVM models are sensitive to outliers and computationally expensive due to numerous support vectors. We thus introduce a Bounding and Minimizing (BaM) loss function, which stabilizes the decision boundary, reduces support vectors, and improves efficiency. This OC-SVM integrated VMSG pipeline generates more interpretable samples. An experimental evaluation of the ASHRAE RP1043/1312 datasets shows that the BaM loss outperforms both hinge and rescaled-hinge losses regarding computational efficiency. Additionally, VMSG outperforms popular minority oversampling techniques, including the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE), its variants, as well as Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) and Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) for fault classification. © 2025 Elsevier Ltd. title: Generative Internet of Things
authors: Maleh Y.; Lamaakal I.; Yahyati C.
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) is evolving. Devices are no longer limited to sensing and reporting. With the rise of generative artificial intelligence (GAI), IoT systems can now create, predict, and adapt. This shift introduces the generative IoT (GIoT). In this article, we introduce the concept of GIoT. We explore how GAI models—such as variational autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, flow-based generative models, and generative diffusion models—enhance IoT in vision, audio, and text-based applications. These models allow devices to understand context, generate content, and make smarter decisions. We also identify major challenges. These include resource limits on edge devices, dynamic network behavior, and data security risks. Finally, we suggest directions for future work to build reliable, efficient, and secure GIoT systems. GIoT has the potential to change how IoT devices operate. This article lays the foundation for that transformation. © 1999-2012 IEEE.

title: GIN-transformer based pairwise graph contrastive learning framework
authors: Zhou S.; Zhou L.; Zhou Y.; Han H.; Zheng H.; Qiao L.
abstract: Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI) provides critical biomarkers for diagnosing neuropsychiatric disorders such as autism spectrum disorder (ASD) and major depressive disorder (MDD). However, existing deep learning models heavily rely on labeled data, limiting their clinical applicability. DCL employs sliding-window augmented rs-fMRI time series, combining GIN for modeling local spatial connectivity and Transformer for capturing global temporal dynamics, enabling multi-scale feature extraction via cross-view contrastive learning. TDF adapts the pre-trained model to downstream classification tasks. We conducted single-site and cross-site evaluation on two publicly available datasets, and the experimental results showed that GITrans-PairCL outperforms both traditional machine learning and deep learning baseline methods in automatic diagnosis of brain diseases. title: PVLM: Parsing-Aware Vision-Language Model With Dynamic Contrastive Learning for Zero-Shot Deepfake Attribution
authors: Zhang Y.; Zhang J.; Ma C.; Guan W.; Gan T.; Gao Z.
abstract: The challenge of tracing the source attribution of forged faces has gained significant attention due to the rapid advancement of generative models. However, existing deepfake attribution (DFA) works primarily focus on the interaction among various domains in vision modality, and other modalities such as texts and face parsing are not fully explored. Besides, they tend to fail to assess the generalization performance of deepfake attributors to unseen advanced generators like diffusion in a fine-grained manner. Additionally, we present a novel deepfake attribution contrastive center loss to pull relevant generators closer and push irrelevant ones away, which can be introduced into DFA models to enhance traceability. title: LiteAugNet: A Lightweight Semantic-Guided Augmentation Network for Efficient Edge-Level Image Classification
authors: Rahman M.S.; Bari M.T.; Nasim Adnan M.; Parvez A.
abstract: Semantic data augmentation offers a principled way to improve robustness in vision models, yet current methods based on large vision–language or diffusion models remain impractical for edge deployment. title: MAESTRO: A Multi-Scale Ensemble Framework with GAN-Based Data Refinement for Robust Malicious Tor Traffic Detection

abstract: Malicious Tor traffic data contains deep domain-specific knowledge, which makes labeling challenging, and the lack of labeled data degrades the accuracy of learning-based detectors. In addition, Tor’s fixed 512-byte cell architecture removes packet-size diversity that many encrypted-traffic methods rely on, making feature extraction difficult. This paper proposes an efficient three-stage framework, MAESTRO v1.0, for malicious Tor traffic detection. title: Confounder-Aware Causal Graph Learning Framework for Multivariate Time Series Analysis
authors: Liu B.; Ma Y.
abstract: Multivariate Time Series (MTS) analysis based graph has gained traction due to complex nonlinear relationships and temporal dependencies among variables. To enhance the interpretability of observational MTS data, causal graph learning has become a mainstream approach. However, existing causal graph methods lack mechanisms to handle unobserved confounders and dynamic causal relationships, which limit their applicability in MTS scenarios. To overcome these limitations, we propose a novel framework, Confounder-Aware Causal Graph Learning (CACGL), which models unobserved confounders with multi-scale effects and captures time-varying causal relationships among variables. Firstly, CACGL employs a multi-granularity causal architecture combining coarse-grained graphs, which model variable-wise causality over entire sequences, with fine-grained graphs that capture cross-variable causal interactions within local segments, explicitly disentangling time-heterogeneous dependencies. Secondly, we design a hierarchical VAE-based module to construct exogeneity-constrained proxies for two unobserved confounders: persistent confounder and transient confounder adhering to causal sufficiency criteria. Third, a bias-aware optimization strategy is proposed to quantify unobserved confounding through the Confounding Bias Index (CBI), which transforms residual confounding effects into adversarial signals to enhance GNN-based causal invariance. In addition, a multi-objective loss is designed to improve the stability of causality, while CBI-driven adversarial learning mitigates confounding bias in downstream tasks. Experiments on real-world datasets demonstrate that CACGL achieves state-of-the-art performance in causal graph discovery for MTS, while modeling time-heterogeneous unobserved confounding and improving interpretability. © 2026 Owner/Author.

title: Confidence-Driven Hybrid Intrusion Detection: Combining Fuzzy Rule Interpolation and Deep Learning
authors: Almseidin M.
abstract: The rapid growth of connected devices has made networks more vulnerable to cyberattacks. While many existing intrusion detection methods have achieved significant results, they often face critical limitations. They often face critical limitations such as low generalization capability, sensitivity to imbalanced data, and high false positive rates. In this article, after thoroughly investigating previous Deep Learning (DL) approaches for intrusion detection, some approaches suffer from overfitting when applied to specific data distributions and lack scalability across diverse datasets. Others rely on computationally expensive feature selection techniques that may not adapt well to dynamic data environments. Some methods, such as GANs and heuristic optimization approaches, address data imbalance issues but can be resource-intensive. Hybrid models such as CNN+RNN and CNN+LSTM often operate as "black box" systems with limited interpretability, making decision-making less transparent. Moreover, many previous studies fail to address uncertainties, including sparse or incomplete training data. To overcome these challenges, in this paper, we propose a novel hybrid intrusion detection approach combining Fuzzy Rule Interpolation (FRI) reasoning and Deep Neural Networks (DNN). FRI’s reasoning engine effectively handles sparse rule issues and enhances adaptability, while the DNN provides high-performance classification. This combination was adapted by introducing the confidence-based fusion parameter. The DNN is used to predict probabilities for different classes, and the highest probability determines how confident the DNN is in its prediction. This confidence level is then used to calculate, which controls how much the final decision relies on the DNN versus an FRI. If the DNN is very confident, its prediction has more weight in the final output. From another perspective, if the DNN is less confident, the system leans more on the FRI. We tested and evaluated the proposed hybrid approach using nine benchmark intrusion datasets, covering various attacks such as IoT attacks, malware, multistep attacks, phishing, DoS, and DDoS. title: A Survey on Acoustic Side-Channel Attacks: An Artificial Intelligence Perspective
authors: Quattrone B.; Badr Y.
abstract: Acoustic Side-Channel Attacks (ASCAs) exploit the sound produced by keyboards and other devices to infer sensitive information without breaching software or network defenses. Recent advances in deep learning, large language models, and signal processing have greatly expanded the feasibility and accuracy of these attacks. To clarify the evolving threat landscape, this survey systematically reviews ASCA research published between January 2020 and February 2025. We categorize modern ASCA methods into three levels of text reconstruction—individual keystrokes, short text (words/phrases), and long-text regeneration— and analyze the signal processing, machine learning, and language-model decoding techniques that enable them. We also evaluate how environmental factors such as microphone placement, ambient noise, and keyboard design influence attack performance, and we examine the challenges of generalizing laboratory-trained models to real-world settings. This survey makes three primary contributions: (1) it provides the first structured taxonomy of ASCAs based on text generation granularity and decoding methodology; (2) it synthesizes cross-study evidence on environmental and hardware factors that fundamentally shape ASCA performance; and (3) it consolidates emerging countermeasures, including Generative Adversarial Network-based noise masking, cryptographic defenses, and environmental mitigation, while identifying open research gaps and future threats posed by voice-enabled IoT and prospective quantum side-channels. Together, these insights underscore the need for interdisciplinary, multi-layered defenses against rapidly advancing ASCA techniques. © 2025 by the authors.

title: ArtGDance: music-driven 3D group dance generation framework
authors: Zhang Y.; Duan R.; Yu H.; Yang K.
abstract: Group dance is a complex and collaborative art form demanding synchronized motion and dynamic spatial coordination, which is intrinsically guided by music’s rhythm, tempo, and emotion. Compared to solo dance generation, group dance generation poses additional challenges: it requires not only generating musically aligned individual motions but also modeling complex inter-dancer interactions, maintaining spatial coherence across multiple performers, and avoiding collisions—all while preserving the artistic expressiveness of the choreography. Extensive experiments on the AIOZ-GDANCE dataset demonstrate that ArtGDance achieves competitive performance in both generation quality and artistic alignment. title: Meta-Learning Driven Voltage Reconstruction and Spatiotemporal Fusion for Battery SOH Estimation Under Incomplete Data
authors: Liu X.; Zhou L.; Tian J.; Wei Z.; Yang J.
abstract: Accurate estimation of state of health (SOH) is a critical challenge in battery management systems. However, in practical operation, charging data is often incomplete due to abnormal operating conditions or limited data access, which reduces the reliability of SOH estimation. To address this issue, an integrated method is proposed for battery SOH estimation by combining data reconstruction with image feature learning. Battery aging data is obtained through aging experiments. A model-agnostic meta-learning-based least squares generative adversarial network (MAML-LSGAN) is developed to reconstruct charging voltage data under different levels of data missingness. The proposed MAML-LSGAN improves the adaptability of voltage reconstruction under different battery aging conditions through meta-learning optimization. Subsequently, the Gramian angular field method is employed to transform the reconstructed 1-D voltage time series into 2-D image representations, enhancing the extraction of aging-related features. On this basis, a Swin transformer-LSTM model integrated with a cross-attention mechanism is constructed to capture spatial–temporal degradation features for accurate battery SOH estimation. The proposed method is validated on two different battery datasets, and experimental results demonstrate that it achieves high SOH estimation accuracy and stability under different training data ratios. © 2020 IEEE.

title: TabDDPM-Aug: Adaptive diffusion-based hybrid augmentation for imbalanced tabular classification
authors: Ahmed T.; Rehman J.U.
abstract: Augmenting imbalanced tabular data is critical for improving classification performance, yet existing generative models face utility-privacy-fidelity trade-offs, particularly when data is limited. They often achieve high utility through memorization or suffer severe distributional collapse. We demonstrate this is not an inherent limitation but a consequence of fixed augmentation strategies that ignore dataset scale, quantified by the minority sample-to-feature ratio ((Formula presented)). We present TabDDPM-Aug, which addresses this through dataset-adaptive strategy selection (DBHA for low-density regimes, FDHA for high-density regimes), Distance-to-Closest-Real (DCR) filtering to eliminate memorized copies, and ensemble generation to prevent mode collapse. Comprehensive evaluation across 13 benchmarks spanning diverse domains, dimensionalities, and imbalance ratios shows TabDDPM-Aug achieves the best average rank on classification utility (rank 1.85 of 9 methods), privacy preservation (rank 1.00), and distributional fidelity (MMD rank 1.46, DCR rank 1.15). In low-density regimes, it maintains competitive utility while achieving up to 48% privacy risk reduction over GAN-based methods. In high-density settings, it yields up to 15% higher F1-score and 94% better distributional fidelity compared to standalone diffusion augmentation on minority samples. These properties make TabDDPM-Aug suitable for fraud detection, healthcare diagnostics, and other privacy-sensitive domains where regulatory compliance is essential. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Empirical comparison of sequence-aware augmentation strategies for real operational AHU AFDD under data scarcity and class imbalance
authors: Wang S.
abstract: Data scarcity and class imbalance remain major challenges in Automated Fault Detection and Diagnosis (AFDD) for Air Handling Units (AHUs), particularly when models are trained using real operational fault data from buildings. This study empirically compares three sequence-aware augmentation strategies for real operational AHU AFDD under different labeled-data regimes: Time-Series (TS)-only augmentation, Trans-CWGAN-only augmentation, and a Hybrid strategy. Experiments were conducted on a fully labeled real operational dataset from 13 AHUs using labeled-data fractions of 30%, 70%, and 100%, and performance was evaluated across Random Forest (RF), TabTransformer, and Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) classifiers. Label scarcity emerged as the primary performance bottleneck, with the macro-F1 score of the Original baseline decreasing from 89.8 at the 70% labeled-data fraction to 69.3 at the 30% fraction. Under severe scarcity (30%), the Hybrid strategy achieved the highest average predictive performance (macro-F1 score: 72.7; accuracy: 77.4), whereas TS-only showed greater robustness and lower sensitivity to hyperparameter settings. Trans-CWGAN-only was the least reliable setting in this regime. At the 70% and 100% labeled-data fractions, the incremental benefit of augmentation diminished and performance approached saturation. Overall, the findings show that augmentation effectiveness is strongly data-regime-dependent. For this single-facility operational dataset, TS-only provides a strong, stable, and low-cost practical baseline under severe scarcity, whereas Hybrid is better interpreted as a conditional option when modest average-performance gains justify additional complexity. © 2026 Elsevier Ltd. title: Over-the-Air Wireless Federated Learning Model for Generative AI
authors: Zheng J.; Niyato D.; Zhang H.; Du H.; Wang J.; Kang J.; Xiong Z.
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) technologies represent an important advancement in the field of AI, particularly for their capabilities in text and image generation. Over-the-air wireless federated learning (OA-WFL) can utilize the wireless waveform superposition property to achieve efficient model aggregation, thereby providing support for GenAI training and deployment. Therefore, this article investigates the support of OA-WFL for GenAI, focusing on potential applications and specific examples. We first discuss the OA-WFL and GenAI models, emphasizing their functionalities and the potential benefits arising from their interaction. We then explore its application in various GenAI scenarios, including large-scale edge device content generation, efficient distributed training of GenAI models, and reduction of bandwidth requirements and device load. Next, a framework is proposed to apply OA-WFL to diffusion models, such as those used in image generation, and validate its effectiveness through simulation results. Finally, we discuss prospective research directions for the application of OA-WFL for GenAI. © 1986-2012 IEEE.

title: Mouse Data Defence Technology Using Machine Learning in Image-Based User Authentication: Based on the WM_INPUT Message
authors: Jung W.; Kim J.; Lee K.
abstract: In personal computers, data is input through devices such as keyboards and mice, and various services are received from the internet. To provide these online services, secure user authentication methods are essential. Knowledge-based authentication methods, such as PINs or passwords, have been widely implemented in most services due to their ease of implementation. However, security threats such as brute-force attacks, phishing attacks, and keyboard data attacks that intercept sensitive user information have emerged. To counter these security threats, image-based authentication methods using mouse input were introduced. However, vulnerabilities arose when functions like GetCursorPos() or WM_INPUT messages were used, allowing mouse input data to be intercepted, thereby undermining image-based authentication. To defend against these attacks, counter-defence methods were developed to generate fake mouse data, protecting actual mouse data. With the advent of these defence methods, there has been a demand for attack methods to classify fake and real mouse data. Recently, machine learning-based methods have been employed on the attacker’s side to classify real mouse data, effectively distinguishing fake from real mouse data and compromising the security of image-based authentication methods. Therefore, this paper proposes a defence technology to safely protect mouse data from theft attacks using machine learning, specifically leveraging Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs). To achieve the goal of this defence technology, the distribution of fake mouse data generated using GANs was analyzed, verifying the feasibility of mouse defence methods. In summary, a system incorporating the defence technology was constructed, and a dataset containing both fake and real mouse data was created. Based on the constructed environment, the performance of the mouse data defence technology was evaluated. The results showed that it reduced performance by up to 37% in the dataset with the highest performance of existing machine learning-based attack methods. This study concludes that the proposed mouse data defence technology effectively addresses vulnerabilities and security threats related to user authentication information in various services relying on image-based authentication methods. © 2025 by the authors.

title: MSSTT-GAN: A CycleGAN with Multi-scale Spatio-Temporal Transformer for Time Series Anomaly Detection in IoT
authors: Jia Y.; Li F.; Zhang J.; Li J.
abstract: Time series anomaly detection has become a key technology for maintaining the stable operation of Internet of Things (IoT) systems by identifying potential faults and security threats. Existing methods face limitations in capturing the temporal correlations, cross-dimensional spatial dependencies, and local dependencies in the high-dimensional time series data from multi-source sensors. We propose an anomaly detection model, MSSTT-GAN, based on Multi-Scale Spatio-Temporal Transformer (MSSTT) and Cycle Generative Adversarial Network (CycleGAN). The model adopts a cycle generative adversarial architecture, integrating the MSSTT module into the generators. The temporal Transformer captures temporal features, while the spatial Transformer analyzes the topological relationships among multiple sensors. A multi-scale patch mechanism is introduced to extract fine-grained features within patch and across patch spatio-temporal associations, enabling local dependency modeling. The discriminators use a spectral normalization convolutional neural network, applying spectral norm constraints to the convolution layers, thus enhancing the stability of adversarial training. The experimental results show that MSSTT-GAN outperforms existing models in terms of F1 score, with an average detection performance improvement of 6.7%. Meanwhile, the Population Stability Index (PSI) is optimized by 87.9%, and the model stability is significantly enhanced. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.

title: Unsupervised Anomaly Detection in Chaotic Time Series Using Brain-Inspired Cortical Coding
authors: Mecik A.B.; Yucel M.; Ustundag B.B.
abstract: Reliable anomaly detection in time series is crucial yet challenging owing to the chaotic nature of signals from sources such as financial markets or natural systems. However, most state-of-the-art approaches rely heavily on extensive parameter tuning and large labeled datasets, which are rarely available in production, making them unsuitable for highly dynamic environments. Because field data are predominantly unlabeled, fully unsupervised anomaly detection has become an operational necessity for practical industrial deployment. We present an enhanced, fully autonomous implementation of the Brain-Inspired Cortical Coding (BIC) framework that effectively eliminates the requirement for manual parameter tuning and labeling. The BIC framework combines adaptive clustering with entropy-oriented cortical coding. Unlike most advanced methods, BIC learns directly from unlabeled data and provides stable performance under varying operational conditions. The evaluation was conducted using synthetic Lorenz attractor signals and real-world artificial intelligence for IT operations (AIOps) key performance indicator (KPI) data characterized by rapidly evolving patterns. The comparative experiments included long short-term memory (LSTM), extreme learning machines (ELM), variational autoencoders (VAE), generative adversarial network (GAN)-based models, Isolation Forest, and statistical baselines. Results show BIC outperforms state-of-the-art models, achieving F1-scores of 0.84 and 0.75 under low- and high-noise Lorenz conditions, and an F1-score of approximately 0.80 on the AIOps KPI dataset across both short and long training regimes. Furthermore, under extended evaluation, BIC maintains stable detection performance, whereas competing models show significant deterioration or require additional retraining. These results demonstrate that BIC provides a robust and scalable solution for anomaly detection in noisy, chaotic, and rapidly evolving time-series environments.  © 2013 IEEE.

title: GAN-KANInformer-Based Prediction of Underwater Temperature-Pressure Sensor Data
authors: Liu H.; Miao X.; Lin Y.
abstract: Accurately predicting short-term changes in interconnected temperature and pressure variables is essential for effective monitoring of subsea oil and gas transportation systems. However, underwater sensor data collected from the field are often limited and show temporal dependencies, nonlinear relationships between variables, and varying operating conditions. To overcome these challenges, this study proposes a two-stage forecasting framework called GAN-KANInformer. First, after splitting the data chronologically, a Wasserstein generative adversarial network with gradient penalty is trained solely on the normalized real training data to generate additional multivariate sequences. The synthetic data are assessed for similarity in distribution, consistency in first differences, preservation of autocorrelation, and maintenance of inter-variable correlation before being combined with the real training samples. Next, the KANInformer model is trained on this augmented dataset, where ProbSparse attention captures temporal interactions and KAN-based nonlinear mappings model the coupled relationships among the thermodynamic variables. Experiments used 1,500 observations recorded every 15 minutes from a temperature and pressure monitoring system in a deepwater oil and gas transport environment at a depth of 1,500 meters. Across ten independent trials, the GAN-KANInformer achieved normalized root mean square errors (nRMSE) of 0.080 ± 0.004, normalized mean absolute errors (nMAE) of 0.062 ± 0.004, and mean absolute percentage errors (MAPE) of 4.820% ± 0.213 for temperature prediction. For pressure prediction, the results were 0.041±0.002 (nRMSE), 0.033 ±0.002 (nMAE), and 4.190% ± 0.181 (MAPE), demonstrating the proposed framework’s effectiveness on this complex dataset under challenging operating conditions. © 2013 IEEE.

title: An Intelligent System for Differentiating Real and AI-Generated Images Using Deep Learning Techniques
authors: Saravanan M.; Venkata Sai Varun Kumar V.; Sai Jawahar Reddy G.
abstract: Most recently, generative models such as GANs and diffusion architectures have developed rapidly enough to appear insane, and indeed so realistic that it is becoming difficult to distinguish between synthetic images and those of real photos. This has struck many subjects we are interested in including the digital forensics, to holding social media accountable and even identity authentication and cyber security. In this task, I am developing a smart system, which will automatically detect whether a picture is a real one or made by an AI using deep learning. I am combining convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with models based on transformers to ensure that we extract both spatial and frequency information that reveals the fact that something is generated. The tool allows uploading of image by file, or taking it by a camera or even URL, thus can be used in vivo. The model performed highly on a dataset consisting of real images and artificial ones generated by StyleGAN, Midjourney and Stable Diffusion, with a high degree of accuracy as well as good robustness. These findings set emphasis on the effectiveness of deep learning in the process of identifying AI-generated texts and why this aspect is important to authenticate digital media and ensure the safety of online environments. © 2026 IEEE.

title: BoneCancerFusionNet: A Multimodal Deep Learning Framework Integrating Medical Images and Clinical Data for Efficient Bone Cancer Detection and Classification
authors: Rao B.D.; Madhavi K.
abstract: Bone cancer is a rare malignancy, with diagnosis presenting a major challenge, and detection having an immense impact on patient prognosis. Existing methods are mainly mono-modal data-driven, i.e., imaging (photo) based or clinical outcome result (procedure or action in text form), discarding the complementary information of the multimodal data. Such complexity, or heterogeneity, in real-world datasets results in low generalisability, and thus, reduced diagnostic performance and misclassification. In order to tackle these challenges, this research proposes a new multimodal learning framework called BoneCancerFusionNet that combines medical images with relevant clinical data to detect and classify bone cancer. This framework uses CNNs to extract features from medical images and MLPs to process clinical data. For intrinsic representation, a tailored feature fusion approach that combines details from both modalities, and an optimized preprocessing pipeline that enhances input content with data augmentation and imputation strategies. The algorithm was validated using the Osteosarcoma-Tumor-Assessment Dataset and resulted in 98.79% accuracy, setting the state-of-the-art record when compared to other established methods (SwarmDL and GAN-based) by significant margins. BoneCancerFusionNets is used for its evaluation and is witnessed to make BoneCancerFusionNET a trustworthy methodology to produce false-negative data and apply augmentations to achieve generalizability across precision, recall, and F1 score. The strength of the standalone multimodal data, as a diagnostic, leads to both qualitative and quantitative AI-based solutions for radiology and clinical decision-making. © 2026 Seventh Sense Research Group®.

title: Survey of Adversarial Example Attack and Defense of Spiking Neural Networks; [脉冲神经网络对抗样本攻击与防御综述]
authors: WANG X.; YUE P.; ZHANG J.; JI J.; DONG H.; KONG D.
abstract: With the wide deployment and application of spiking neural networks, their security problems have become more and more obvious, especially the threat from adversarial example attacks. Therefore, the adversarial example attack methods and defense measures in spiking neural networks are investigated. Firstly, the adversarial sample attack methods are studied, and the software layer is sorted out from the gradient attack, migration learning attack, encoding perturbation attack and sensor attack. The hardware layer deals with power injection attack, side channel attack and Trojan horse attack. Secondly, the defense measures of adversarial samples are studied. The defense measures of the software layer are sorted from adversarial training, input filtering, improved coding, feature network analysis and model fusion. The defense measures of hardware layer are discussed from two parts of circuit optimization and security framework. Then, the application of adversarial examples in model security research and CAPTCHA anti- identification is discussed. Finally, the current challenges and future prospects are put forward and the whole paper is summarized.

title: LR-WGAN: A Multivariate Time-Series Imputation Scheme Based on Low-Rank Matrix Completion and Wasserstein GAN for Industrial IoT
authors: Awaisi K.S.; Ye Q.; Sampalli S.
abstract: Multivariate time-series data from industrial sensor networks are often affected by missing values due to communication failures, sensor malfunctions, and network delays. Accurate imputation is essential for reliable monitoring and decision-making in Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) systems. In this paper, we propose Low-Rank matrix completion-assisted Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (LR-WGAN), a scheme for imputing missing values in multivariate time-series industrial sensor data. The proposed framework integrates Low-Rank Matrix Completion (LRMC), Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (WGAN), and Transformer-based encoders to capture both sensor-specific temporal dynamics and global inter-sensor dependencies. Instead of relying on random noise, the generator receives structured low-rank pre-imputed sequences for coherent initialization. The architecture includes a Temporal Encoder and a Spatio-Temporal Encoder, while a time-decay mechanism is used to model irregular temporal gaps. The discriminator employs a Transformer encoder and utilizes both imputed values and observation masks. Experiments on the Skoltech Anomaly Benchmark (SKAB) dataset and the Appliances Energy Prediction dataset show that LR-WGAN achieves lower RMSE and competitive MAE across multiple missingness scenarios. Specifically, under MCAR at 10% missingness, LR-WGAN achieves RMSE values of 0.0619 on the SKAB dataset and 0.0377 on the Appliances Energy Prediction dataset, indicating stable and accurate imputation performance.  © 2015 IEEE.

title: ResProto-FD: Visual-Language Residual Prototype Sets for Generalized Face Forgery Detection
authors: Jing J.; Zheng Y.; Peng C.
abstract: With the rapid development of generative models, such as generative adversarial networks and diffusion models, the task of face forgery detection has emerged, aiming to identify forged faces in real-world scenarios. A key challenge for current face forgery detection models is improving generalization to unknown forgeries. To address this, we propose ResProto-FD, a framework that constructs residual prototype sets to capture diverse forgery cues and discriminative differences from real faces. Our novel perspective collects prototypes from the most informative residual features generated during training, enabling better representation of various forgery traces and real-vs-fake distinctions. First, we introduce a Visual-Language Residual Learning (VLRL) module based on the CLIP model. This module constructs residual features between image and text embeddings to capture inconsistencies between visual features and associated textual semantics. In doing so, it guides the model to attend to subtle visual forgery clues and enhances the discriminative power of image representations. Furthermore, we design a Gradient-aware Residual Prototypes (GRP) mechanism— a dynamic collection strategy that selectively stores uncertain residual features based on gradient signals to build the prototype sets. This enhances the model’s ability to generalize to unknown forgery types. Extensive experiments across various datasets and forgery methods demonstrate that ResProto-FD significantly improves generalization performance and consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. © 2026, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (www.aaai.org). title: Intelligent Time Series Prediction and Anomaly Detection Method and Engineering Validation for Industrial Scenarios of Mobile Oil Pipelines
authors: Zhang Y.; Zhao R.; Yang Q.
abstract: Mobile oil pipelines are the core equipment of the emergency oil support and field oil transportation system, and their transportation safety and stability determine support mission execution efficiency. Aiming at problems in existing anomaly detection methods under unsteady conditions, strong interference, and small abnormal sample scenarios, this paper proposes an AI time series prediction and anomaly detection method integrating hydraulic mechanism prior knowledge. The method constructs a time - frequency hybrid attention time series prediction model with dual constraints to achieve high - precision short - term prediction of pipeline key parameters under unsteady conditions. It designs a prediction - reconstruction dual - path collaborative anomaly detection framework driven by a task - aware gating network to accurately identify both sudden and gradual anomalies. A mechanism - constrained time series generative adversarial network is proposed to augment abnormal data in small sample scenarios and improve model generalization. Ablation experiments verify the necessity of the dual - path framework and the effectiveness of the gating network, and supplementary sensor fault simulation experiments prove the method's engineering robustness. Engineering validation on a 5 km pipeline shows that the proposed method has a pressure prediction MAPE of 2.15% under sudden condition changes, an overall anomaly detection accuracy of 98.2%, and a false alarm rate of 0.32%, significantly outperforming existing mainstream methods. The research results can support the intelligent operation and maintenance of mobile oil pipelines and provide a reference for intelligent anomaly detection in similar unsteady industrial scenarios. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Privacy-Preserving PMU Data Recovery Using Independent Federated GMHAT – BiLSTM Considering DoS Attacks and PMU Failure
authors: Haghdar K.; Fotuhi-Firuzabad M.; Abbaspour A.; Wang F.; Dehghanian P.
abstract: As Phasor Measurement Units (PMUs) become integral to real-time state estimation within the evolving cyber-physical infrastructure of smart grids, they are increasingly susceptible to data anomalies and cybersecurity vulnerabilities. Ensuring uninterrupted and secure grid operations necessitates robust mechanisms for recovering data following anomaly detection. Existing recovery techniques, however, are often hindered by elevated computational complexity and suboptimal performance, especially under widespread anomalies, while centralized architectures exacerbate systemic risks through single points of failure. To mitigate these deficiencies, an independent federated privacy-preserving data recovery framework leveraging Graph Multi-Head ATtention (GMHAT) – Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) mechanisms is introduced. The GMHAT-BiLSTM with sliding data window captures both temporal and spatial dependencies in PMU time-series data to enable accurate data recovery. Evaluations on data from the IEEE 39-bus benchmark system, Texas A&M University electric grid test dataset and real-world experimental data collected from the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory microgrid validate the performance of proposed independent federated structure and GMHAT-BiLSTM, outperforming conventional federated structure, Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Transformer and convolutional neural network (CNN)-LSTM networks under multiple operational scenarios in terms of mean absolute error, root mean square error and coefficient of determination. © 2010-2012 IEEE.

title: Synthetic Data Augmentation for COD Prediction in WTTPs: A Comparative Study of Deep Learning Models with VARMA and TTS-GAN

abstract: Data scarcity poses a significant challenge in time series forecasting using Deep Learning (DL), particularly in wastewater treatment, where data are scarce, infrequent, and often operationally constrained. title: ARGUS: A Robust Guard for Mobile Crowdsensing User Registration
authors: Eryonucu C.; Papadimitratos P.
abstract: Mobile Crowdsensing Systems (MCS) can be attacked by an adversary that registers numerous fictitious, typically emulated, devices to report bogus data in large volumes. It is crucial to safeguard MCS by preventing registration of fictitious devices, broadly termed Sybils. Most existing defenses try to detect Sybils essentially too late, after the adversary succeeds in having them join and after having influenced the system; more so, they require sensitive user information or demand burdensome manual tasks, ultimately discouraging participation. This is why we introduce ARGUS as an early screening mechanism that thwarts attempts to register Sybils at a high rate at the first stage of user registration. ARGUS reduces the fictitious device registration rate by filtering out their registrations early in their interaction with the system, before their adversarial data can influence the MCS. To sift fake/Sybil users, we utilize sparsely sampled smartphone battery logs to reflect actual user and smartphone usage characteristics without exposing privacy-sensitive information. ARGUS isolates and identifies even (colluding) Sybil users orchestrated by an attacker with a high volume of synthetically generated data. ARGUS leverages well-known machine learning components in a novel way and provides protection for systems without relying on historical user data or user interaction (as required, notably, by CAPTCHA); that is, without reducing privacy, inconveniencing users, or discouraging participation. We evaluate the effectiveness of ARGUS through extensive experiments, demonstrating it consistently achieves an F1-score greater than 90% in detecting a broad range of Sybil registrations; with adversarial strategies ranging from perturbing genuine traces to training generative adversarial networks (GANs). Unlike existing defenses that verify device integrity (e.g., device attestation) or human presence (e.g., CAPTCHA), both of which are susceptible to high bypass rates under certain attacks, ARGUS assesses behavioral authenticity through battery usage patterns, without user interaction and pre-emptively, offering a new, fundamentally orthogonal, and complementary countermeasure. Lightweight and easy to deploy, ARGUS is the first method to leverage mobile device battery traces to detect Sybil attacks in MCS systems without exposing privacy-sensitive user data. ARGUS can significantly increase the cost for any adversary that seeks to introduce Sybils at a high rate, effectively and efficiently detecting and rejecting those that result from adversarial automation and generated data.  © 2013 IEEE.

title: Automated Deepfake Content Detection using GAN-based Analysis and Temporal Models
authors: Mesia Dhas J.T.; Venkata Sesha Surya P.; Manohar C.
abstract: The enhanced pace of the generative artificial intelligence has significantly contributed to the degree of authenticity of the synthetic text, image, audio, and video contents, posing serious threats to the digitally trusted, cybersecurity and authenticity of the online information. Visual artifacts are extracted using convolutional neural networks that operate on frequency domain analysis. The resulting representations of the modality is then combined with the help of the attention-based multimodal learning strategy which enables effective correlations of the heterogeneous features. It has been shown with empirical tests on publicly available benchmark datasets that the proposed framework can be utilized to achieve superior detection performances, as well as superior cross-dataset generalization, as compared with unimodal baselines. title: Can Generative Adversarial Networks Compete against Diffusion Models at Generating Time Series?
authors: Engler P.; van Elst L.; Ahmed S.; Dengel A.
abstract: Diffusion models have become the state-of-the-art at synthetic data generation, widely replacing generative adversarial networks (GANs) in recent years. GANs often suffer from issues like training instabilities and mode collapse. However, they also offer advantages. They are computationally efficient, as they only require a single forward pass for generating a synthetic data sample. Thus, we ask the question whether GANs can still compete with diffusion models. Specifically, we tackle the task of generating conditional time series—one of the most common data modalities in industrial applications. Making a model follow conditions appropriately is not always trivial. In this work, we leverage a structured noise space (SNS) to implicitly condition GANs for generating time series data. The SNS allows to use an unconditional generator architecture for conditional data generation by training it on a certain latent space structure. We extensively evaluate the method on time series datasets from the UCR classification archive, comparing to other GAN, variational autoencoder and diffusion approaches. We find advantages over explicit conditioning regarding fidelity of generated samples and training stability. With our improved architecture, we show that SNS-GAN is able to compete with diffusion at a fraction of the sampling time. Additionally, we examine limitations and propose alternatives of structuring the noise space so that the model can effectively learn the condition in varying scenarios. © 2026 by SCITEPRESS – Science and Technology Publications, Lda.

title: Quantum Wasserstein GAN: A Novel Approach for Generating Anomalous Timeseries Data
authors: Kumar S.; Kulkarni S.G.
abstract: Anomaly detection in time series is constrained by the scarcity and unpredictability of real anomalous events. Classical supervised and generative approaches struggle to capture the statistical complexity of rare, high-impact anomalies while maintaining realistic normal dynamics. This work introduces a Quantum Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network (QWGAN) for synthetic anomaly generation that separates the modeling of normal and anomalous behaviors using quantum parameterized circuits. Leveraging quantum superposition and entanglement, the QWGAN achieves a richer generative capacity with an order-of-magnitude reduction in parameters compared to classical counterparts. The model is trained and evaluated on cyber security datasets, demonstrating lower Earth Mover's Distance and volatility error while preserving temporal structure and distributional fidelity. A windowed synthesis mechanism enables controlled injection of variable-length point and contextual anomalies. Our results demonstrate that QWGAN provides a scalable, parameter-efficient approach for generating high-fidelity synthetic anomalous time series data to enable effective benchmarking and augmentation of anomaly detection models under limited anomaly data. © 2026 IEEE.

title: MelShield: Robust Mel-Domain Audio Watermarking for Provenance Attribution of AI Generated Synthesized Speech
authors: Jin Y.; Li Q.; Liu L.; Ni J.
abstract: In this paper, we propose MelShield, a robust, in-generation, keyed audio watermarking framework that embeds identifiable signals into AI-generated audio for copyright protection and reliable attribution. Specifically, MelShield operates in the Mel-spectrogram domain during the generation process, targeting intermediate acoustic representations in Mel-conditioned pipelines for text-to-speech (TTS) generation. The core idea is to treat the intermediate Mel-spectrogram as the host signal and embed a short binary payload via low-energy, keyed spread-spectrum perturbations distributed across carefully selected time-frequency regions prior to waveform synthesis. By performing watermarking before vocoder inference, MelShield remains plug-and-play for Mel-conditioned TTS architectures and does not require modification or retraining of the underlying TTS generation vocoder, such as DiffWave and HiFi-GAN. Moreover, the multi-user keyed construction enables scalable user-specific attribution, while the keyed verification mechanism limits unauthorized decoding, thereby reducing the risk of large-scale extractor probing and adversarial analysis. Extensive experiments on DiffWave and HiFi-GAN demonstrate that MelShield achieves reliable watermark extraction, approaching 100% bit accuracy, even under signal distortions, e.g., compression and additive noise, while preserving high perceptual audio quality. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.
