title: Quantum Generative Adversarial Networks for EEG-Based Sleep Stage Classification in Noiseless and Noisy Scenarios
authors: Passo S.J.G.; Khan I.U.; Prevost J.J.
abstract: Sleep disorders affect about one billion people worldwide, yet automated sleep staging is limited by class imbalance in polysomnographic datasets and the representational capacity of classical generative models. This work compares a classical Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) with two Quantum Wasserstein GAN-GP (QWGAN-GP) variants - noiseless and noisy simulator - for synthetic EEG augmentation in sleep stage classification using the ANPHY-Sleep dataset [1]. Models are trained under a Wasserstein GAN with Gradient Penalty (WGAN-GP) across subsets of 2-4 statistical EEG features over 50 epochs. Results show consistent quantum-enhanced variance matching: QWGAN-GP variants achieve lower standard deviation mean absolute error (StdMAE) than the classical GAN, with reductions up to 70.9% at 3 features. The 6-qubit generator (26 = 64-dimensional Hilbert space) captures EEG variance more faithfully than a classical multilayer perceptron. Moderate Gaussian noise (σ = 0.1) during QGAN training acts as implicit regularisation, yielding the best StdMAE (0.064) and competitive classification (Accuracy = 0.880, F1 = 0.880). The classical GAN suffers mode collapse at higher dimensions, dropping to 0.535-0.585 accuracy, while the noiseless QGAN reaches 0.905 at 3 features. A downstream classification evaluation on real PSG labels confirms that the quantum generator preserves N1 minority-class F1 (up to 0.1053 at 4 features) where the classical GAN consistently collapses to N1 F1 = 0.000 across all feature configurations. These results demonstrate that hybrid quantum-classical generative models provide a structurally distinct and empirically superior approach for minority-class distribution learning in imbalanced clinical time-series, albeit with higher classical simulation overhead.  © 2026 IEEE.

title: DeepAnom: A Hybrid Time GAN and LSTM Autoencoder Framework for Time-Series Anomaly Detection in IIoT Systems
authors: Joshi M.M.; Monish L.; Sowbhagya M.P.; Mekali V.; Manjula M.; Nagratana N.
abstract: Data represented in the form of a time series appears in many fields, including finances or health care, or in industries where the role of detecting anomalies becomes crucial for guaranteeing stability. However, it appears that the reason behind such high importance of anomaly detection comes from the fact that its lack might result in many problems. Unfortunately, anomaly detection models often fail due to the problem of lack of correctly labeled datasets for training purposes. For this reason, it is recommended to use Time GAN model, i.e., time series generative adversarial network for creating synthetic data sets which would help to improve anomaly detection. The idea of Time GAN lies in combining the methods of adversarial training and supervised learning, thus adding to the model both the temporal component and relevant features. Such a method allows for learning the time series patterns without just copying them. When a dataset is created using a Time GAN model, it can be included into the existing datasets to make further improvements to training. Experiments have shown that incorporating synthetic data into a model improves anomaly detection accuracy and robustness.  © 2026 IEEE.

title: A Multi-Step Prediction Method Based on Small Sample Data Augmentation to Assess Wheat Flour Safety Risk
authors: Sheng W.; Jiang H.; Pi W.; Yang Z.; Zhao L.
abstract: Food safety significantly impacts the human health, establishing an effective prediction method to assess food safety risk is crucial for food safety control. At present, in the situation of insufficient detection data, it is necessary to employ data augmentation methods to generate large-scale detection data and accurately capture the long-term variation patterns through safety risk prediction models. However, existing data augmentation methods and safety prediction models face challenges such as gradient vanishing and difficulty in capturing long-term dependencies. Therefore, this paper proposes a Small sample Data Augmentation Multi-step Prediction Method (SDAMPM) to assess wheat flour safety risks. Firstly, we improved time-series generative adversarial networks based on external temporal convolution and Wasserstein distance to expand wheat flour hazard factor detection data. Secondly, we employed expanded data to establish dietary exposure evaluation system for wheat flour, serving as the desired output for multi-step prediction models. Finally, we constructed a stable Informer (Stainformer) multi-step prediction model by designing symmetric ProbSparse self-attention and distilling layer based on dilated causal convolution. Experiments on the wheat flour dietary exposure evaluation system demonstrate that compared to other methods, the expanded data is similar to the distribution of the original data. This approach effectively predicts long-term safety risks associated with wheat flour consumption and can provide assistance and technical support in decision-making for relevant departments, thereby reducing the occurrence of food safety incidents. © 2013 IEEE.

title: Physiology-Informed Diffusion for 12-Lead ECG Generation
authors: Yehuda Y.; Radinsky K.
abstract: Large-scale 12-lead ECG data are critical for training reliable cardiac machine learning systems, yet their availability is limited by privacy constraints, annotation cost, and severe class imbalance. Generative models offer a promising solution, but standard diffusion models typically treat ECGs as generic multivariate time series and do not explicitly exploit known physiological structure. We propose PhysDiff-ECG, a physiology-guided diffusion framework that integrates cardiac ordinary differential equation (ODE) prior into the diffusion trajectory. Our central idea is to make ECG physiology tractable during training by deriving differentiable regularizers from a dynamical model of cardiac activity together with a differentiable 12-lead observation model. Given a denoised reconstruction along the reverse process, PhysDiff-ECG fits a latent physiological explanation via an unrolled inner optimization and penalizes violations of both the simulator dynamics and the induced ECG reconstruction. This training-time regularization biases the learned denoising trajectories toward physiologically realizable ECGs while preserving the flexibility of latent diffusion. Experiments on standard 12-lead ECG benchmarks show that PhysDiff-ECG improves physiological fidelity, representation-space realism, class-conditional diagnostic consistency, and downstream classification performance relative to strong GAN and diffusion baselines. © 2026, Transactions on Machine Learning Research. title: Generative Adversarial Networks with Gated Recurrent Units for Stock Return Modelling and Portfolio Management Using Synthetic Financial Time Series
authors: Goyal A.; Golash R.; Kumar A.
abstract: Portfolio optimisation is one of the main tasks in investment to maximise returns while minimising risk under given constraints. However, real-time market conditions and geopolitical factors affecting the financial markets are rapidly changing, and thus long-term historical data become less reliable for capturing current dynamics. Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) offer a solution by generating synthetic financial data that reflects realistic market behaviour. To address this, we propose a Gated Recurrent Unit-based GAN (GRU-GAN) with Wasserstein Distance (WD) loss, a sequential GAN designed to generate synthetic financial time-series data by capturing temporal dependencies in stock returns, such as those from major US tech companies (AAPL, MSFT, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). The performance metrics demonstrate that the proposed GRU-GAN outperforms the V-GAN, achieving a higher annualised return (2.3624 vs. 1.5054) and a superior Sharpe Ratio (7.3852 vs. 4.1680), reflecting better risk-adjusted returns. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: AGC-WGAN: Adaptive granularity conditional Wasserstein GAN for time series forecasting using multivariate data
authors: Pattanaik S.; Das D.; Roy D.S.; Barik R.K.
abstract: The proposed work presents a comprehensive framework for multi-horizon time-series forecasting and synthetic data generation using an adaptive Granularity Module. We utilise the Earth-Mover’s Distance (Wasserstein-1 metric), which efficiently mitigates mode collapse by ensuring smoother critic gradients. To preserve Lipschitz continuity without limiting network weights, a Gradient Penalty regularisation scheme is additionally implemented, resulting in stable critic updates. A lightweight gated recurrent neural architecture, Fast-GRNN, with a Three-Layer Cascading architecture, is also suggested for temporal representation learning and long-term dependencies. Strong alignment between synthetic and real data distributions is demonstrated by experimental evaluations, which achieve competitive metrics, including the KS Statistic (0.28-0.35), JS Divergence (0.32-0.39), Wasserstein Distance (0.36-0.56), Pearson Correlation (up to 0.18), and MMD (0.07-0.20). Additionally, with MSE values ranging from 0.0535 to 0.1833 and MAE values ranging from 0.1995 to 0.3472 across Users, Packets, and Bytes, our forecasting model achieves low out-of-sample errors on the test set. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Scenario-Based Forecasting of Epidemics Using Generative AI and Traditional Methods: An Empirical Evaluation on Epidemiological Data
authors: Oliinyk Y.; Pentiuc S.-G.
abstract: The COVID-19 time series are characterized by non-stationary dynamics and volatile spikes, making traditional deterministic models fragile when data distributions shift. This paper presents a comparative evaluation of generative artificial intelligence architectures, including Convolutional Transformers, Variational Autoencoders (VAE), and Time-series Generative Adversarial Networks (TimeGAN) against traditional machine learning regressors for epidemic forecasting. The study analyses point predictions as well as the generation of probabilistic scenarios: optimistic, probable, and pessimistic. To address model heterogeneity, a Robust Median Ensemble is introduced to construct a consensus meta-scenario, providing stability and outlier immunity against individual model failures. Experimental results using COVID-19 data from Romania demonstrate that while traditional methods remain computationally competitive, generative models, particularly when enhanced by TimeGAN-driven synthetic data augmentation, offer significant advantages in quantifying uncertainty. title: Audio Adversarial Example With No Noise in the Silent Area for Speech Recognition System
authors: Ko K.; Kim S.; Kwon H.
abstract: In this paper, we propose a specific type of adversarial example which is recognized appropriately by humans and is misrecognized by the target model and is generated by adding adversarial noise only to that part of the original audio sample that contains an audio signal. The method adds noise only to the part of the audio containing a voice signal in such a way that human can identify the resulting sample correctly but the target model will misclassify. The proposed method is distinguished from existing methods for generating adversarial examples in that it adds adversarial noise only to that portion of the audio file in which an audio signal appears; this distinction gives it the advantage that in the resulting sample, it is nearly impossible for a human to identify the adversarial noise. Our experiments used the Mozilla Common Voice dataset, with a Deep Speech model. The results demonstrate that the proposed method of generating adversarial examples achieved a success rate of 91.4% in attacking the target model, while keeping the average distortion from the original sample to a minimum value of 232.20. © 2013 IEEE.

title: Synthetic Sensor Data Augmentation using Generative Adversarial Networks for Improving Industrial Asset Reliability in Predictive Maintenance - A Systematic Review
authors: Mhetre S.; Shinde S.; Patil P.; Narwade P.; Ramse P.; Patil R.
abstract: Predictive Maintenance (PdM) is a critical strategy for industrial operators and reliability engineers, enabling them to forecast the remaining useful life (RUL) of assets in manufacturing, energy and aerospace industries. Contributing to reducing the downtime by usage of sensor time-series data. The PdM paradox- Due to the scarce amount of minor class data or run-to-failure data from cost and safety constraints, leads to the creation of imbalanced datasets in which there is less than five percent fault samples. The systematic review examines the use of generative adversarial networks (GANs) for synthetic sensor data augmentation in PdM, guided by PRISMA principles. Sequential run-to-failure trajectory generation with advances in multi-modal fusion is demonstrated by a taxonomy of GAN variants, including vanilla and conditional GANs, TimeGAN, and Wasserstein GANs with gradient penalty, This results in ten to thirty-five percent improvements in accuracy, F1-score, and RUL estimation over baselines like SMOTE on benchmarks like C-MAPSS and IMS. Training instability, mode collapse, and explainability deficiencies in multisensor scenarios are major obstacles. The review provides a pros-and-cons analysis, points out physical plausibility gaps, and describes future directions with a focus on explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) integration through techniques like SHAP for reliable augmentation and physics-informed GAN hybrids for unseen conditions. The synthesis aligns with the Industry 4.0 applications for developing interpretable frameworks. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Review of development and application of deepfake face detection technology; [深度伪造人脸检测技术发展与应用综述]
authors: Li W.; Feng Y.; Hou B.; Jiao L.
abstract: With the rapid maturation and democratization of deep learning technologies, deepfake generation has evolved from a niche technical curiosity into a pervasive global phenomenon. As these tools become increasingly accessible, forged images and videos are proliferating across the Internet at an unprecedented scale. Among these, deepfake images and videos targeting human faces—particularly those involving identity manipulation of public figures and celebrities—are frequently exploited for malicious intent. These applications range from defamation and nonconsensual pornography to the manipulation of public opinion and the dissemination of disinformation, and thereby pose severe threats to digital trust, individual reputation, and social stability. Consequently, the development of robust deepfake face detection (DFD) technology has emerged as a critical research frontier and a strategic priority for the academic community and the industrial sector. This review provides a systematic, comprehensive survey of the current landscape of DFD, with a specific focus on the prevalent manipulation technique of face swapping. The paper first scrutinizes the evolution of underlying generation mechanisms, detailing typical forgery methods including variational autoencoders, generative adversarial networks, and the emerging diffusion models. According to changed attributes, face forgery methods can be classified into four common forms—facial transfer, facial swapping, facial reenactment, and facial editing. Subsequently, the review proposes a structured taxonomy of detection methodologies and categorizes them into three primary streams based on model architecture—CNN-based methods, Transformer-based methods, and the new paradigms. CNN-based methods currently represent the mainstream approach. This paper analyzes their diverse structural characteristics and further subdivides them into six distinct subcategories based on their feature extraction strategies, such as basic CNN architecture and frequency domain analysis. This paper also analyzes the advantages, disadvantages, and applicable scenarios of each structure. This work highlights Transformer-based methods for their recent rapid advancement. This review discusses the Transformer-based detection models in two branches. One type consists solely of the Transformer structure. By adding modules and enhancing the structure, the detection accuracy and computing efficiency can be improved. CNN-Transformer hybrid architecture makes full use of the local receptive field of the CNN architecture and the global modeling capability of the Transformer. The new paradigms section explores innovative innovations, specifically self-supervised/unsupervised learning combined with large language models (LLMs). The paper elucidates how self-supervised/unsupervised learning mitigates the dependency on labeled data and effectively avoids the overfitting bias caused by specific datasets or forgery types. Furthermore, this paper examines how integrating LLMs introduces semantic understanding and text features and significantly enhances the generalization capabilities and the interpretability of detection decisions. In the domain of data infrastructure, the paper traces the evolution of deepfake datasets and contrasts classic datasets, which rely solely on visual data (images or videos), with the new generation of multimodal datasets that have emerged over the past two years. These modern datasets, enriched with human annotations and descriptive text prompts, are pivotal for training more context-aware detection models and thereby fundamentally redefine the objective from simplistic perceptual categorization to a more demanding exercise in cognitive reasoning and contextual justification. By using the multimodal dataset to enhance, the interpretability of the detection method will be improved. Evaluation is also a critical component of this survey. The paper provides a comprehensive summary of evaluation metrics, distinguishing between classification performance, generalization performance, and practical deployment metrics. While acknowledging that DFD is a binary classification task, common classification evaluation metrics can be used. Considering the particularity of the DFD task, in general cases, an imbalance exists between the true and false categories of the data samples, and some metrics such as accuracy have certain limitations. Therefore, this paper advocates adopting more reliable metrics. Regarding generalization, the paper details protocols for cross-forgery and cross-dataset evaluation, which are essential for measuring robustness against unseen attacks. Generalization is an indispensable indicator during model evaluation, especially in the current era where forgery techniques are diverse and rapidly evolving. Additionally, considering application requirements such as real-time monitoring on edge devices, the review summarizes efficiency metrics, including inference speed, memory footprint, and parameter count, which are important in the model during deployment. Moreover, from an application perspective, DFD technology can be used to prevent the spread of false information and to stop criminals from using deepfake face technology to steal people’s information, property, and other targets. Thus, this review synthesizes four major deployment scenarios—verification of media content authenticity, protection of digital identity security, judicial evidence collection/forensics, and the automated supervision of social network content. In parallel, this work reviews the developing legal landscape, specifically domestic regulations governing deep synthesis services, and highlights the intersection of technology and law. Finally, based on a dialectical analysis of the primary contradictions in the field (such as the failure of detection features due to the evolution of generation technology and insufficient data-driven and generalization capabilities) this paper identifies critical future trends—the deeper integration of detection systems with LLMs, the pursuit of explainable, highly generalizable detection models to enhance trust, model lightweighting for edge device deployment, and the continuous refinement of industry regulations to govern the ethical use of synthetic media. In summary, the DFD technology, as a core technology for safeguarding the truth and trust in the digital age, is currently in a stage of rapid evolution and multidisciplinary integration. DFD is worthy of researchers’ investment of time and effort for research and advancement. title: Design of Experiments for Pix2Pix Hyperparameter Analysis in Energy Consumption Data Imputation
authors: De Rezende J.A.M.; Teixeira E.H.; Otávio de S.M.G.; Pimenta T.C.
abstract: The occurrence of missing values in time series is a recurring problem caused by sensor failures or communication losses, compromising the quality of data-driven analyses. This work investigates the influence of Pix2Pix Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) hyperparameters on the imputation of missing values under different missing data mechanisms. Using the Electricity Load Diagrams 2011-2014 dataset, 40% of the observable values were artificially removed according to the Missing at Random (MAR), Missing Completely at Random (MCAR), and hybrid (MAR+MCAR) mechanisms. The Design of Experiments (DOE) approach was employed to systematically evaluate the effect of the Pix2Pix GAN hyperparameters on the Adjusted Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (ASMAPE). In addition to identifying the combination of learning rate and number of steps as the most influential hyperparameters in imputation performance, the results showed that the model maintains similar performance under different missing data mechanisms, highlighting the robustness and reliability of the Pix2Pix GAN in imputation tasks. The study contributes a statistically grounded methodology for hyperparameter analysis in energy consumption time series. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Detecting and Preventing Deepfake Phishing Using GAN Fingerprinting
authors: Yadav N.; Malik K.; Indra G.
abstract: Deepfake phishing attempts use artificial intelligence (AI) generated synthetic fake content to trick users into revealing private information. These sophisticated threats are difficult for traditional cybersecurity methods to identify. In order to identify and stop deepfake phishing, this research suggests a GAN fingerprinting technique. We enhance the accuracy and traceability of detection by incorporating synthetic fingerprints into phishing content produced by GANs. To distinguish between genuine and fake phishing attempts, we use fingerprinted datasets to build a convolutional neural network (CNN) model. High detection accuracy and resilience to hostile attacks are demonstrated by the experimental results. A proactive approach to reducing the hazards of deepfake phishing is provided by the suggested solution. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Switzerland AG 2026.

title: A^{2}RA-NSMTSllm: Adversarially Aligning Retrieval-Augmented LLMs for Nonstationary Multivariate Time Series Forecasting
authors: Chu J.; Liu C.; Bai X.; Tan J.
abstract: Multivariate time series (MTS) forecasting is critical in various real-world applications. Recent studies leverage large language models (LLMs) for MTS forecasting, achieving impressive improvements in prediction accuracy and generalization over deep learning-based models. However, these methods often overlook the inherent nonstationarity and domain-specific nature of MTS, as well as the MTS-text modality representation gap, thus limiting the full potential of LLMs in MTS forecasting. In this article, we present A^{2}RA-NSMTSllm, a novel multiscale model that adversarially aligns retrieval-augmented LLMs for nonstationary MTS forecasting (A^{2}RA-NSMTSllm). Specifically, A^{2}RA-NSMTSllm employs a frequency-guided multiscale decomposition normalization–denormalization Framework, which adaptively removes and recovers the nonstationarity based on multiscale distribution dynamics modeling. To bridge the gap between MTS and LLM semantic space, it develops a time series–text alignment reconstruction-enhanced generative adversarial network, where the generator effectively learns to produce LLM-friendly TS embeddings without losing key temporal features. Furthermore, A^{2}RA-NSMTSllm introduces a TS knowledge base retrieval-augmented mechanism to enhance domain-specific forecasting, dynamically retrieving and integrating relevant knowledge to guide LLM temporal reasoning and forecasting. Extensive experiments show that A^{2}RA-NSMTSllm achieves superior forecasting performance and generalization, outperforming the latest CALF by 8.19%/5.27%, 11.01%/8.66%, and 20.94%/10.84% in MSE/MAE across full-shot, few-shot, and zero-shot scenarios. © 2005-2012 IEEE.

title: Introduction to AI-generated Image and Video Synthesis
authors: Mewada A.; Aquib Ansari M.; Ahmad S.; Singh N.
abstract: The rapid development of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has revolutionised the creation of synthetic visual art, including images, videos, and animation models generated using deep learning (DL) models. This chapter provides an overview of the underlying technologies, including Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs), Variational Autoencoders (VAEs), diffusion models, and transformer-based architectures, which enable the generation of photorealistic photos and videos. It covers important methods, such as text-to-image, style transfer, super-resolution, deepfake technologies, motion transfer, and video prediction, along with their applications in the real world, including creative industries, healthcare, scientific visualisation, gaming, and education. The chapter also addresses serious issues, including semantic consistency, temporal coherence, information bias, and the legal and ethical implications of synthetic media, misinformation, intellectual property, and regulatory lapses. In the future, it will discuss the new trends in real-time generation, controllability, integration with AR/VR, and research questions that are open to exploration. Through an analysis of the transformative potential and societal risks, this chapter highlights the importance of responsible development and use of AI-generated media technologies. title: Advanced Intrusion Detection in Wireless Sensor Networks Using Vanilla Generative Adversarial Network
authors: Kalita B.; Sarmah S.; Singh B.K.
abstract: Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are increasingly vulnerable to sophisticated cyber-attacks, while intrusion detection systems (IDS) often suffer from limited and imbalanced training data. Traditional Machine Learning (ML)-based approaches fail to effectively detect minority and zero-day attacks due to insufficient representation in datasets. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a Vanilla Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based data augmentation framework to enhance intrusion detection performance in WSNs. The GAN model generates realistic synthetic network traffic samples to balance minority attack classes. The augmented dataset is then evaluated using a Gradient Boosting (GB) classifier on the WSN-DS dataset. Experimental results demonstrate significant improvement in detection performance, achieving an overall accuracy of 96.74% and F1-score of 96.74%, with notable enhancement in minority attack detection such as Grayhole (97.44%) and Blackhole (97.76%). The results confirm that GAN-based data augmentation improves robustness and generalization of IDS models while effectively addressing class imbalance in WSN environments. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Universal Adversarial Purification with DDIM Metric Loss for Stable Diffusion
authors: Zheng L.; Xie L.; Zhou J.; Yimin H.
abstract: Stable Diffusion (SD) often produces degraded outputs when the training dataset contains adversarial noise. Adversarial purification offers a promising solution by removing adversarial noise from contaminated data. However, existing purification methods are primarily designed for classification tasks and fail to address SD-specific adversarial strategies, such as attacks targeting the VAE encoder, UNet denoiser, or both. To address the gap in SD security, we propose Universal Diffusion Adversarial Purification (UDAP), a novel framework tailored for defending adversarial attacks targeting SD models. UDAP leverages the distinct reconstruction behaviors of clean and adversarial images during Denoising Diffusion Implicit Models (DDIM) inversion to optimize the purification process. By minimizing the DDIM metric loss, UDAP can effectively remove adversarial noise. Additionally, we introduce a dynamic epoch adjustment strategy that adapts optimization iterations based on reconstruction errors, significantly improving efficiency without sacrificing purification quality. Experiments demonstrate UDAP’s robustness against diverse adversarial methods, including PID (VAE-targeted), Anti-DreamBooth (UNet-targeted), MIST (hybrid), and robustness-enhanced variants like Anti-Diffusion (Anti-DF) and MetaCloak. UDAP also generalizes well across SD versions and text prompts, showcasing its practical applicability in real-world scenarios. © 2026, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (www.aaai.org). title: McGAN based data reconstruction between heterogeneous phased arrays for 2D DoA estimation
authors: Liu S.; Hu B.; Li L.
abstract: In order to facilitate Direction-of-arrival (DoA) estimation for irregular phased arrays, a multi-label conditional Generative Adversarial Network (mcGAN) is proposed to conduct data reconstruction between two heterogeneous arrays. First, system model for data reconstruction between heterogeneous phased arrays is established. A target array is designed with the same array aperture as the source array. Afterwards, data preprocessing is performed. The normalized real and imaginary data of the source array covariance matrix are set as input to the mcGAN generator. At the same time, the covariance matrix of the target array is specified as the generator's output. The signal DoAs are used as multi-labels whose label dimension is twice the number of signals. To avoid information leakage, the multi-dimensional labels are only fed into the discriminator but not the generator. Finally, an appropriate DoA estimation algorithm is applied to yield the DoA estimates. An example of UCA to L-shaped array data transformation is demonstrated. Simulation results have verified the efficiency and accuracy of the irregular to regular, high-dimensional to low-dimensional data reconstruction carried out by the proposed mcGAN. It is revealed that mcGAN can accurately control the generation of expected patterns without pattern mismatch and shows good generalization abilities. © 2026 IEEE.

title: From VoiceFlow to VoiceFlow++: Stochastic Duration and GAN Refinement for High-Quality TTS
authors: Wang Q.; Yang F.; Xu Y.
abstract: Although diffusion models have approached humanlevel performance in text-to-speech (TTS) tasks, their iterative inference process-often requiring hundreds of steps-remains a bottleneck for real-time deployment. VoiceFlow addresses this issue by leveraging flow matching and flow rectification to compress sampling into just 2-10 steps, enabling high-quality speech synthesis at low step counts. However, this method requires frame-level duration annotations prior to training and relies on deterministic duration prediction, limiting its ability to model natural rhythm variations and reducing flexibility. To overcome these limitations, we propose VoiceFlow++, which introduces a stochastic duration predictor, the Monotonic Alignment Search algorithm, and adversarial training to achieve expressive, highfidelity, and ultra-fast speech synthesis. Experiments on the LJSpeech and LibriTTS datasets demonstrate that VoiceFlow++ can generate natural and expressive mel-spectrograms with minimal inference steps, significantly outperforming existing fast TTS methods. Our approach provides a scalable and efficient framework for real-time deployment in interactive systems. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Generative AI for FinTech
authors: Dubey M.
abstract: Recent advancements in generative artificial intelligence (AI) have introduced novel opportunities for the application of AI within the financial sector. This chapter examines the various ways in which generative AI is contributing to the rapidly evolving landscape of finance. While traditional machine learning techniques have long been applied to financial tasks such as customer service, text summarization, risk prediction, algorithmic trading, and document processing, generative AI offers enhanced capabilities aimed at improving operational efficiency, elevating customer experience, and enabling responsible growth. Applications of generative AI in finance now extend to areas including decision-making, risk assessment, portfolio optimization, personalized financial advising, fraud detection, and predictive analytics. The field encompasses a diverse set of models, including generative adversarial networks (GANs), variational autoencoders (VAEs), temporal point processes (TPPs), transformers, and large language models (LLMs). This chapter explores how these models are applied in financial contexts, highlighting both theoretical foundations and practical implementations. A dedicated case study is presented, summarizing recent literature on the use of LLMs in financial tasks, including approaches such as zero-shot and few-shot learning with pretrained models, domain-specific fine-tuning, and training models from the ground up. Finally, the chapter discusses key opportunities and challenges associated with generative AI in FinTech, including the balance between innovation and responsibility, and the need for enhanced interpretability, robustness, and ethical compliance in financial applications, hence aiding towards goals of Industry 5.0. © 2026 selection and editorial matter, Sangeeta Sharma, Robin Singh Bhadoria and Mukesh Kumar Giluka; individual chapters, the contributors.

title: Adaptive Time Series Data Augmentation via MemFormer: Memory-Augmented and Reinforcement Learning-Driven Generation
authors: Huang B.; Shi H.; Liu W.; Ma R.
abstract: Time series forecasting is crucial across various domains but is often hindered by data scarcity, limiting model efficacy. Generative models, particularly GAN-based approaches, have been widely explored for data augmentation; however, they struggle to capture intricate temporal dependencies and recurrent patterns, often failing to produce diverse and high-fidelity synthetic data. To address these challenges, we propose MemFormer, a memory-augmented generative model tailored for time series augmentation. MemFormer integrates a Transformer backbone with an adapter-memory module, enabling the efficient storage, retrieval, and consolidation of both short- and long-term temporal patterns. Moreover, we formulate noise sampling as a reinforcement learning problem to enhance the diversity of generated samples. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that MemFormer produces more realistic and varied time series data, leading to significant improvements in downstream forecasting tasks, particularly in low-data regimes. These results position MemFormer as a state-of-the-art solution for time series data augmentation. © 2026 IEEE.

title: ICIP: An integrated approach for AI image generation using stable diffusion

title: A Deep Learning Based Intrusion Detection Framework for Smart Grids using CGAN, CNN, and SVM
authors: Slama M.B.; Bouazzi A.; Wajdi S.; Abdelhamid H.
abstract: Smart Grids (SG) are critical infrastructures that integrate advanced communication technologies such as 4 G, 5G, 6G, and the Internet of Things (IoT) to improve energy management and system efficiency. Common attacks include denial-of-service (DoS/DDoS) attacks and malware, which can seriously compromise network reliability and security. To address these challenges, efficient intrusion detection systems (IDS) are required. In this work, we propose an IDS framework based on deep learning and machine learning techniques. Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) are used to generate synthetic data in order to enhance the training process and mitigate data imbalance. Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) are employed for automatic feature extraction, while Support Vector Machines (SVM) are used for intrusion classification. Experimental results show that the proposed approach improves detection performance and enhances the robustness of the IDS in Smart Grid environments. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Evaluating Stable Diffusion with LoRA for Class-Imbalanced Medical Image Augmentation
authors: Ahmed S.; Aspia J.F.; Kapali B.R.; Rahman K.; Murad M.S.
abstract: Deep learning models for medical image analysis are frequently constrained by severe class imbalance and data scarcity, especially in clinical settings where positive cases are rare. Although GAN-based synthesis and classical augmentation have been investigated to address these problems, they often have poor scalability under real-world restrictions, low diversity, and training instability. In this study, we thoroughly assess text-to-image Stable Diffusion as a useful data augmentation technique for class-imbalanced medical imaging. Using renal stone CT imaging as a case study, we optimize Stable Diffusion with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) to produce high-quality synthetic samples exclusively for the minority class. Instead of suggesting a new classifier, we evaluate the created data's usefulness using many standardized downstream evaluation backbones, such as CNN and transformer-based models, to guarantee robustness among representation learning paradigms. Comprehensive tests and ablation studies on synthetic-to-real data ratios show that while excessive dependence on synthetic data worsens performance due to distributional bias, moderate diffusion-based augmentation (25 -50%) consistently increases recall and F1-score. Qualitative analysis and Fréchet Inception Distance enhance the realism of the generated visuals. Overall, this study demonstrates that, under realistic data and computational restrictions, Stable Diffusion, when modified via LoRA, can function as an efficient but limited data augmentation technique for class-imbalanced medical imaging. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Triple Bridge Cross Domain Recommendation Integrating Adversarial Networks and Contrastive Learning; [融合对抗网络和对比学习的三重桥梁跨域推荐]
authors: YANG H.; MEI H.; HU S.
abstract: A triple bridge cross domain recommendation model (ACTBCDR) that integrates adversarial networks and contrastive learning is proposed to address the problems of negative preference modeling deficiency and single user preference transfer strategy in existing meta learning cross domain recommendation methods. Positive and negative feature encoders are designed to obtain users’positive and negative preferences, in order to capture more comprehensive user preferences. title: Deep Learning-Based Enhanced Predictive Modeling for Stock Price
authors: Halder S.; Sarkar P.; Chakraborty T.; Mondal K.C.
abstract: The prediction of financial markets using deep learning has attracted the attention of both investors and researchers. Deep learning methods, such as convolutional neural networks and recurrent neural networks, work well at predicting stock indices based on the non-linear characteristics of stock markets. title: Adaptive Rhythm Control Optimization via Multi-Source Keyboard Performance Data Fusion for Intelligent Music Production
authors: Li H.
abstract: This paper proposes an adaptive rhythm control optimization framework based on multi-source keyboard performance data fusion. This framework primarily addresses the challenge of rhythm modeling in intelligent music generation relying on a single modality and failing to characterize the dynamic features of performance. The method first constructs a unified multi-source rhythm representation space, encoding the symbolic layer, acoustic layer, behavioral layer, spatial layer, and control layer across modalities. Based on this, a five-dimensional fusion tensor structure is designed. This innovation enables strict alignment of multi-source data in the temporal dimension and completes temporal calibration of heterogeneous data through cross-source neighborhood consistency constraints. Furthermore, a multi-source attention fusion mechanism is introduced. This mechanism models the cooperative and conflict relationships between different modalities through interaction terms. At the rhythm modeling level, this study proposes a fusion-driven beat fingerprint function. This process characterizes the acceleration features of rhythm changes through multi-source response weighting and second-order time derivative enhancement terms. Simultaneously, cross-source consistency constraints are combined to improve the stability of multi-modal responses. At the generation and control layers, a hidden Markov rhythm dynamic model under fusion feature conditions is constructed. Simultaneously, the variational autoencoders and Wasserstein generative adversarial networks are combined to achieve rhythm latent space modeling and distribution alignment. Finally, the fused features are introduced into the reinforcement learning control framework. The experiments were conducted using the self-built multi-source keyboard performance dataset MKPD-Set. Results show that, compared to single-modal fusion methods, the proposed method reduces beat offset error (BOE) by approximately 28.2%. It also achieves significant improvements in rhythm consistency (FC) and generation diversity (GD). Even under 30% noise conditions, rhythm accuracy (RA) remains at a high level. abstract: This paper introduces a novel Temporal-Attention Generative Adversarial Network (TA-GAN) framework for stock market prediction that addresses the inherent challenges of financial time series forecasting, including non-stationarity, high volatility, and complex temporal dependencies. title: Prompt-guided synthetic data generation to mitigate domain shift in periapical lesion detection
authors: Özüdoğru S.; Coşkun F.Ö.; Uysal F.; Küçüktaş Ü.T.; Hardalaç F.; Kaya D.I.
abstract: Objectives: Domain shift—the mismatch between training and deployment distributions—degrades deep learning at inference. Vision-language foundation models (VLMs) like ChatGPT-4o generalize out-of-distribution and enable controllable image-to-image synthesis, but direct clinical use is costly and, when closed-source, raises privacy concerns. We instead use a VLM to guide synthetic data generation, strengthening smaller deployable detectors without task-specific retraining—a controllable substitute for generative adversarial network (GAN)/ diffusion augmentation, which typically requires large domain-specific datasets and unstable training. We use panoramic radiographs to compare a prompt-guided approach with an expert-guided classical image-processing baseline under morphology/size shift. Methods: A dataset of 196 panoramic radiographs (145 annotated, 51 healthy) was used. We implemented two transparent augmentation pipelines: (i) Expert-Guided Synthesis (EGS), where clinicians delineated lesion masks that were procedurally rendered (noise-based texture, intensity modulation, edge blending); and (ii) Prompt-Guided Lesion Synthesis (PGLS), where clinicians specified lesion attributes via text prompts (size, shape, margin sharpness, contrast, location) and ChatGPT-4o produced parameterized image-to-image edits. A You Only Look Once (YOLO)10 detector was trained under three regimes (Real-only, Real+EGS, Real+PGLS) and evaluated with five-fold cross-validation and size-stratified reporting (small/ medium/large). Size-stratified baselines: small—0.30/0.085/0.27; medium —0.58/0.26/0.50; large—0.46/0.20/0.49. Both synthetic strategies improved robustness; PGLS consistently exceeded EGS. Overall, EGS 0.50/0.25/0.52 (+6.4%/ +13.6%/ +10.6%), PGLS 0.51/0.26/0.53 (+8.5%/ +18.2%/ +12.8%). title: Collision Detection and Body-Part Classification in Collaborative Robots Using a Multi-Task Deep Learning Model With Hybrid Time-Series Augmentation

abstract: Ensuring collision safety in human–robot collaboration has emerged as a critical challenge in the Industry 5.0 era. title: The Resilience of Pix2pix in Energy Consumption Data Imputation: Beyond Statistical Significance

abstract: Missing values in time series data, often caused by sensor failures, can compromise the reliability of data-driven analyzes. While Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) such as Pix2Pix have proven effective for data imputation, their evaluation typically relies on null hypothesis significance testing (NHST), which is a practice often criticized for its dichotomous focus on pvalues. This study advocates for and applies an estimation-based statistical framework emphasizing effect sizes and compatibility intervals to provide a more informative assessment of model robustness. We evaluated the imputation performance of Pix2Pix on an energy consumption dataset under twelve experimental conditions, varying the missing data mechanisms: Missing at Random (MAR), Missing Completely at Random (MCAR), and a hybrid MAR+MCAR. Additionally, missingness rates ranged from 20% to 80%, with 30 independent repetitions per condition. Performance was measured using the Adjusted Symmetric Mean Absolute Percentage Error (ASMAPE). The results demonstrate that Pix2Pix maintains overall robustness under all experimental conditions. Although the hybrid MAR+MCAR mechanism exhibited the highest variability of performance, estimationbased analyses using 95% compatibility intervals indicated that the mean performance differences across all conditions were practically negligible. These findings confirm the resilience of Pix2Pix for complex imputation tasks and underscore the value of estimation-based 'new statistics' approaches over traditional NHST in providing a more comprehensive characterization of model performance and uncertainty. © 2026 IEEE.

title: SG-HAT: Semantic-Guided Hybrid-Attention Transformer for Unsupervised Video Summarization

abstract: Video summarization (VS) aims to generate a representative summary of original video content, thereby promoting research in social behavior prediction and analysis. Meanwhile, we are motivated to explore the intrinsic thematic consistency across different modalities. Based on this, we propose an unsupervised VS method termed the semantic-guided hybrid-attention transformer (SG-HAT). Building upon the SUM-GAN-AAE framework, we replace the traditional LSTM-based architecture with an encoder-decoder Transformer to capture thematic consistency. Specifically, we incorporate FSA into the decoder, enabling both local and holistic perception by measuring the similarity between frame-level and global features. In addition, multihead cross-attention enables effective cross-modal interaction. By adding FSA into the frame selector, we construct a semantically driven GAN training strategy to achieve precise video reconstruction. Furthermore, with the help of vision-language models, we introduce textual information by generating dense captions and text summaries for each video in the TVSum and SumMe datasets. title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Cybersecurity:: Protecting Data and Networks
authors: Chandra Blessie E.; Raj P.; Sundaravadivazhagan B.
abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) play a crucial dual role in cybersecurity, serving both as powerful defensive tools and sophisticated attack vectors that security professionals must understand and counter. GANs are invaluable for generating synthetic datasets to train cybersecurity models when real attack data is scarce or sensitive, creating realistic network traffic patterns for testing intrusion detection systems, and augmenting threat intelligence by simulating various attack scenarios without exposing actual vulnerabilities. Exploring the application of GAN models in intrusion detection, anomaly detection, and cybercrime, Generative Adversarial Networks for Cybersecurity: Protecting Data and Networks covers how GANs can be applied to pinpoint security holes, vulnerabilities, viruses, malware, phishing attacks, and other security risks. It explains how advanced GANs integrated with such digital technologies as the Internet of Things (IoT), cloud-native computing, edge analytics, serverless technology, and blockchain to protect and secure data and information from security breaches. The book also discusses how GANs can identify outliers, performance bottlenecks, and other issues in cloud infrastructure modules, applications, and data. Other topics featured in the book include: GAN-based security’s ethical and privacy concerns GANs and explainable artificial intelligence (AI) Building trustworthy sixth-generation (6G) networks with Generative Adversarial Learning (GAL) Intrusion detection systems enhanced by GANs GANs are a valuable tool for enhancing cybersecurity efforts by generating synthetic data and images that can show unusual patterns in data. This book helps researchers, academics, and professionals realize the potential of this powerful tool by presenting the latest innovations and applications of GANs in cybersecurity. © 2026 selection and editorial matter, E. title: Early Transient Fault Diagnosis Framework for Wind Turbine via Sparse Multi-View Learning
authors: Xu Q.; Yang T.; Sun X.
abstract: Transient faults are important early indicators of potential failures in wind turbines, and their timely detection is crucial for reducing unplanned downtime and maintenance costs. However, traditional approaches encounter significant challenges because transient fault signals are typically short in duration, sparse in features, weak in amplitude, and highly susceptible to interference and randomly missing data. To address these issues, this paper proposes a sparse multi-view learning framework that explicitly reveals weak one-dimensional features through two-dimensional representation, and integrates fine-grained texture attention and adversarial learning for feature enhancement and classification, enabling accurate identification of transient faults in wind power systems. Specifically, an improved Intertemporal Return Plot (IRP) is employed to convert short-time multi-source sensor data into two-dimensional multi-view images, which are further augmented by an improved Wasserstein generative adversarial network for fine-grained sample generation. A hierarchical texture attention feature module (HTAFM) is then designed to enhance the model's sensitivity to sparse and subtle features. Finally, a locally adaptive Kolmogorov-Arnold Network (KAN) is incorporated to improve discriminative capability under conditions of missing data. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly outperforms existing approaches in fault detection accuracy. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Optimal design models for visual communication: image generation based on variational autoencoders
authors: Cai L.; Arshad M.
abstract: Amidst the rapid evolution of modern visual design and human-computer interaction, the automatic synthesis of high-fidelity images from natural language descriptions has emerged as a pivotal research frontier in artificial intelligence within the domain of visual communication. Conventional text-to-image generation techniques continue to grapple with limitations in semantic-visual alignment, image fidelity, and model controllability, rendering them insufficient for complex, multi-scene, and multi-semantic generation tasks. In this study, we introduce Variational-Contrastive Learning Generative Adversarial Network (VCL-GAN). This novel image generation framework synergistically integrates a variational autoencoder with a contrastive learning paradigm to address the core challenges of language-driven image synthesis in visual communication optimization. Built upon the GAN architecture, the proposed model employs a dual-path semantic encoding strategy within the generator, wherein text representations derived via Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) are simultaneously infused into both a canonical semantic path and a structured latent path facilitated by the variational autoencoder (VAE). To further enrich semantic granularity, we incorporate cross-modal and intra-modal contrastive losses, thereby enhancing semantic coherence and perceptual fidelity in the generated outputs. Extensive experiments conducted on two benchmark datasets, Caltech-UCSD Birds (CUB) and Microsoft Common Objects in Context (MS-COCO), demonstrate that VCL-GAN surpasses state-of-the-art models such as AttnGAN in terms of Inception Score (IS) and Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), while also exhibiting superior robustness and generalizability in subjective user evaluations and ablation studies. The proposed approach not only advances the precision, clarity, and semantic richness of language-conditioned image generation but also presents a compelling paradigm for intelligent visual communication systems, holding significant promise for applications in Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted design, cultural content creation, and multimodal human-computer interaction. title: Spatiotemporal Prediction of Strong Earthquake Risk in the Sichuan-Yunnan Region Using a GAN-RNN Fusion Model
authors: Qiao L.; He S.; Zhang L.
abstract: This study addresses the low generalization and insufficient accuracy of traditional seismic risk analysis caused by limited strong earthquake samples. A strong earthquake risk assessment framework is proposed for the Sichuan-Yunnan region using 1956 - 2024 seismic catalogs, integrating spatiotemporal distribution analysis, GAN-based data augmentation, RNN time series prediction, and provincial boundary-constrained risk mapping. Experiments show that earthquakes in the region exhibit a west-high and east-low pattern, with shallow-focus events clustering along major faults. The GAN-generated samples achieve over 92% distribution consistency with real records. The GAN-RNN fusion model outperforms standalone RNN, LSTM, and GRU models in accuracy and stability. High-risk zones are mainly located in the Ganzi - Aba fault zone and Kunming - Dali - Lijiang region. This work provides support for regional seismic risk identification, disaster mitigation planning, and engineering seismic design.  © 2026 IEEE.

title: Time-Series Generative Modeling for Characterizing the Output Uncertainty of Newly Deployed PV Stations in IoT-Enabled Distributed Energy Systems
authors: Li Y.; Liang Z.; Chung C.Y.; Fu X.; Yin X.; Zhu J.
abstract: The extensive deployment of photovoltaic (PV) resources in internet of things (IoT)-enabled distributed energy infrastructures, such as smart homes, smart buildings, and consumer-side energy management systems, intensifies the need for accurate characterization of output uncertainties, particularly for newly commissioned PV stations with extremely limited historical data. However, conventional sampling-based and forecasting-based approaches tend to perform poorly under sparse data conditions. This study addresses these limitations by proposing a time-series generative adversarial network (GAN) framework for the generation of high-quality PV-output scenarios even under sparse data conditions. The GAN framework replaces the conventional adversarial discriminator with a non-parametric maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) criterion to minimize statistical divergence between real and synthetic distributions directly. In addition, the proposed MMD-TimeGAN approach integrates an embedding-recovery network architecture with a recurrent generator. The joint optimization of this integrated architecture enables the model to generate realistic, temporally consistent PV-output scenarios. Moreover, this design enhances training stability, mitigates mode collapse, and improves sample efficiency significantly under few-shot learning conditions. The results of extensive case studies obtained using real-world solar datasets demonstrate that the proposed framework consistently outperforms current state-of-the-art GAN-based approaches in both full-data and 7-day few-shot scenarios. The proposed framework provides a robust and practical solution for high-quality synthetic scenario generation, enabling reliable data augmentation and risk-aware energy management under data scarcity in IoT-enabled distributed energy systems.  © 2014 IEEE.

title: A Location Based Secure File Sharing System Using Cryptography
authors: Suryakala K.; Tamilkodi R.; Sarita K.; Deviprasad P.; Raju K.M.; Satish T.
abstract: The exponential growth of digital communication has drastically transformed the way sensitive information is exchanged over the internet. While cloud platforms and centralized servers have made file storage and transfer more accessible, they also introduce serious concerns regarding privacy, data integrity, and unauthorized access. This paper proposes a novel Location-Based Secure File Sharing System using Cryptography that integrates Generative Adversarial Network (GAN)-based encryption, AES encryption, locationlocking mechanisms, and real-time anomaly detection with XG Boost. Unlike conventional cryptographic systems that rely only on encryption strength, the proposed approach enforces access control based on the geographical position of the user, verified through GPS coordinates A unique file ID (8 characters alphanumeric) and a 16-character hashed access key are generated for every uploaded file, while a separate 8-character private key is provided to the uploader to reconstruct the original file from the decrypted text. To ensure robust anomaly detection, the system continuously monitors access attempts and applies machine learning techniques to identify suspicious activities in real time. By combining cryptography, AI-driven anomaly detection, and geospatial security, the proposed system achieves a higher level of confidentiality, authenticity, and resilience against cyber-attacks. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the system achieves low false-positive rates in anomaly detection, high accuracy in location validation, and reliable encryption performance, making it a viable solution for industries requiring secure data transfer, such as healthcare, defense, and finance.  © 2026 IEEE.

title: Generative AI Approaches for Synthetic Health Data Generation: Methods, Applications, and Challenges
authors: Vanitha V.; Srivani M.
abstract: Generating realistic synthetic health data using Artificial Intelligence models offers a powerful solution to privacy restrictions and data scarcity in healthcare. Modern generative frameworks such as Generative Adversarial Networks, Variational Autoencoders, diffusion models, and transformer-based language models enable the synthesis of diverse clinical data, including structured EHR tables, time-series vitals, unstructured clinical notes, and medical images. These models are evaluated on fidelity, utility, and privacy, with applications ranging from data augmentation to privacy-preserving data sharing. GANs excel at learning joint distributions, VAEs capture smooth latent structures, diffusion models yield high-fidelity samples, and transformers produce coherent medical text. Challenges remain in ensuring clinical validity, diversity, and robust privacy protection while avoiding biases and mode collapse. Emerging research explores multimodal generation, promising richer, more integrated synthetic patient records that can transform healthcare research and AI model development. title: Research on Intrusion Detection for Vehicle CAN Bus Based on AAFormer-GAN
authors: Liu C.
abstract: With the rapid development of the intelligent connected vehicle industry, the number of on-board ECUs has surged. As the core standard for on-board communication, the CAN protocol faces prominent security risks. Bus intrusion can easily lead to vehicle loss of control and other accidents, making the research and development of on-board network intrusion detection technology of great significance. This paper expounds on the structure of the CAN protocol, the classification of intrusion detection systems, and the core characteristics of CNN. Addressing the bottlenecks of data imbalance in datasets and unknown attack detection, we design a data generation network based on the associative attention mechanism, AAFormer-GAN. This network, with AAFormer as its backbone, employs a mean squared error loss function to alleviate the vanishing gradient problem in traditional GANs, generating time-series attack samples that closely resemble the real distribution. Experimental verification shows that its generation quality surpasses mainstream models such as WGAN-GP. The unknown attack detection model constructed based on this provides an innovative solution for onboard CAN bus intrusion detection, enhancing the ability to identify small samples and unknown attacks. © 2026 IEEE.

title: Study on the Localization Technology for Giant Salamanders Using Passive UHF RFID and Incomplete D-Tr Measurement Data
authors: Sun N.; Lu D.; Yang X.; Gao H.; Chen J.
abstract: To enhance the monitoring and conservation efforts for China’s Class II endangered species, specifically the wild giant salamander and its ecosystems, this study addresses the urgent need to counteract the rapid decline of its wild population caused by habitat loss and insufficient surveillance. We present an innovative localization system based on passive Ultra-High-Frequency Radio Frequency Identification (UHF RFID) technology, employing a Double-Transform (D-Tr) methodology that integrates an enhanced 3D LANDMARC algorithm with GAIN generative adversarial networks. This system effectively reconstructs missing Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) data due to environmental barriers by applying a log-distance path loss model. The D-Tr framework simultaneously generates RSSI sequences alongside their first-order differential characteristics, allowing for a comprehensive analysis of spatiotemporal signal relationships. Field tests conducted in the Hubei Xianfeng Zhongjian River Giant Salamander National Nature Reserve reveal that the positioning error consistently remains within 10 cm, with average accuracy improvements of 20.075%, 15.331%, and 12.925% along the X, Y, and Z axes, respectively, compared to traditional time-series models such as long short-term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrent unit (GRU). This system, designed to investigate the behavioral patterns and movement paths of farmed giant salamanders, achieves centimeter-level tracking of their cave-dwelling activities. It provides essential technical support for quantitatively assessing their daily activity patterns, habitat choices, and population trends, thereby promoting a shift from passive oversight to proactive monitoring in the conservation of endangered species. © 2025 by the authors.

title: SAFE: Semantic-and Frequency-Enhanced Curriculum for Cross-Domain Deepfake Detection
authors: Yao Y.; Zheng K.; Wu B.; Wu C.; Wang J.; Gao J.; Yang M.; Luo D.
abstract: Driven by advances in GANs and diffusion models, deepfake content has reached an unprecedented level of photo-realism, causing detectors to deteriorate once they leave their training domain. Most prior studies adopt CLIP as the backbone of an image-level binary classifier, yet overlook CLIP’s core strength: text-to-image semantic alignment. Moreover, captions generated by CLIP-CAP lack sufficient high-level semantics to distinguish between authentic and manipulated faces. Deepfake generators often fail to maintain semantic coherence, resulting in contradictions that traditional visual models cannot capture. Existing approaches also intermingle all samples during training and thus lack a systematic, difficulty-aware curriculum. To bridge these gaps, we introduce Semantic-and Frequency-Enhanced (SAFE) deepfake detection, a two-component framework: 1) Semantic-enhanced multimodal alignment. Authenticity cues are injected into CLIP-CAP captions, and low-rank LoRA fine-tuning is applied to CLIP’s visual branch, yielding dual supervision for text–image alignment and forgery discrimination. 2) Dual-score curriculum learning. Fourier Correlation Variance (FCV) measures local spectral consistency and, combined with the loss value, is transformed into a difficulty score that ranks training samples from easy to hard, reducing training time by 23.3% and enhancing generalization. SAFE attains state-of-the-art performance on several cross-dataset and cross-manipulation benchmarks. Ablation studies confirm that semantic enhancement, LoRA fine-tuning, and dual-score curriculum are complementary, jointly delivering substantial gains in open-set generalization. © 2026, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (www.aaai.org). title: Power Grid Anomaly Detection Based on Transformer Architecture with Sparse Attention and Self-Supervised Learning
authors: Jin Y.; Yao H.; Liu X.; Zhang H.; Wang Y.; Zhao F.; Wang R.
abstract: Power grid anomaly detection is crucial for maintaining electrical system stability and preventing potential failures. Traditional statistical methods and conventional machine learning approaches often struggle with the complex temporal dependencies and high-dimensional characteristics inherent in power consumption data. This paper proposes a novel anomaly detection framework that integrates Transformer architecture with sparse attention mechanisms, self-supervised learning, and Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) for enhanced power grid anomaly detection. Our approach leverages the self-attention mechanism of Transformers to capture long-range temporal dependencies while employing sparse attention to reduce computational complexity and focus on the most relevant time steps. The self-supervised learning component enables the model to learn meaningful representations from unlabeled data, while the GAN framework provides additional discriminative power for anomaly identification. Extensive experiments conducted on the London Household Electricity Consumption (LCL) dataset demonstrate the superiority of our proposed method, achieving remarkable performance metrics: Precision of 0.9550, Recall of 0.8833, F1-Score of 0.9177, and AUC of 0.9525. Comprehensive comparisons with baseline models including LSTM, CNN, and AutoEncoder variants, along with detailed ablation studies, validate the effectiveness of each component in our integrated framework. The results indicate that our approach significantly outperforms traditional methods and provides a robust solution for real-world power grid monitoring applications. © The Author(s), under exclusive license to Springer Nature Singapore Pte Ltd. 2026.

title: A systematic review on computer vision-based methods for cervical cancer detection
authors: Mbelwa H.; Leo J.; Kahesa C.; Mkoba E.
abstract: Cervical cancer is a leading cause of mortality among women globally, especially in regions where access to timely screening remains a challenge. With such concerns, accurate detection of cervical lesions is essential for effective diagnosis and treatment. This review aimed to explore the application of computer vision-based methods for detecting cervical cancer, identifying their potential, setbacks and areas for future development. A comprehensive literature search across Scopus, IEEE Xplore, PubMed, and Google Scholar identified 96 relevant studies published between 2014 and August 2025. These studies applied computer vision methods including CNNs, Vision Transformers, and multimodal models to cervical cancer detection using Pap smear, colposcopy, and histopathology images. They were analyzed based on the techniques employed, datasets used, evaluation metrics adopted, and reported results. This review highlights significant advancements in the field, particularly in lesion classification, precise segmentation of affected regions, and accurate detection of cancerous regions. However, some challenges were identified, including limited image datasets with insufficiently distributed normal and abnormal cases, aggravated by privacy issues and accurate labeling of medical images, which is critical and rigorous, often leading to annotation inconsistencies. Lastly, this study revealed that integrating Natural Language Processing and Computer Vision can enhance cervical cancer diagnosis through multi-modal models that combine both clinical text and imaging data. Additionally, this study proposes the use of techniques like annotation-efficient learning to manage limited labeled datasets using methods such as semi-supervised and transfer learning as well as the use of federated learning to ensure privacy in computer-aided diagnostic systems. © 2025 The Authors.

title: Air Quality Monitoring and Forecasting Using Deep Learning
authors: Vanitha T.C.; Sadashiva S.; Pramodhini R.
abstract: Urban air pollution from rapid urbanization, industrial growth, and vehicle emissions poses severe risks to public health, including respiratory illnesses and reduced lifespan. Conventional monitoring relies on costly reference stations with poor spatial coverage, while low-cost IoT sensors generate noisy data affected by drift, spikes, and gaps. This study introduces a software-simulated IoT framework for air quality monitoring and AQI forecasting that overcomes these issues without physical hardware. Virtual sensors replicate real-world imperfections like Gaussian noise, temporal drift, outliers, and missing values on public datasets (e.g., UCI Air Quality). Rigorous preprocessing applies interpolation, smoothing, and Min-Max normalization, followed by GAN-based augmentation (TimeGAN variant) to expand limited datasets while preserving temporal patterns - validated via KS tests and TSTR benchmarks. Advanced models including LSTM is trained for multi-step AQI prediction, achieving low RMSE/MAE and high R2. Visual dashboards display trends, forecasts, and comparisons, enabling actionable insights for smart cities. The proposed system employs Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks as the primary forecasting model, selected for their superior ability to capture long-range temporal dependencies in multivariate pollutant time-series. Results confirm superior robustness over baselines, offering a scalable, cost-free solution for environmental management. © 2026 IEEE.

title: A WGAN-GP Extreme Wind Power Scenario Generation Method Based on Persistent Homology Feature Constraints
authors: Yang T.; Xiong T.; Qin S.; Zou H.; Huang A.; Lou S.
abstract: The transition toward decarbonized energy systems relies heavily on the large-scale integration of wind power, introducing stochastic volatility that challenges traditional grid planning paradigms. While standard stochastic optimization relies on scenario generation, capturing extreme scenarios - rare, high-impact events located in the distribution's long tail - remains a formidable challenge. Conventional Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) often suffer from "distribution smoothing,"failing to reproduce the sharp gradients and complex morphologies of extreme events. This paper presents a comprehensive methodology: a Conditional Wasserstein GAN with Gradient Penalty (cWGAN-GP) augmented by Persistent Homology (PH) constraints. By integrating Topological Data Analysis (TDA) to extract robust geometric invariants from wind power time series, and utilizing a differentiable proxy network (TopoNet), this approach enforces morphological fidelity in generated scenarios. The analysis demonstrates that this topologically regularized framework significantly outperforms baselines in reproducing the statistical, temporal, and physical characteristics of extreme wind power events, providing a critical tool for robust power system risk assessment.  © 2026 IEEE.

title: Forecasting Voltage Time Series under Anomalies Using a WGAN Model With Lipschitz Control and Progressive Kernel Critic Strategy
authors: Safarabadi, Sadat, Najmieh
abstract: In time-series forecasting tasks, the use of recursive forecasting on high-dimensional data substantially increases the complexity of the prediction process. The main challenge is that long-term dynamics becomes harder to model, since the sequences show greater temporal variability. To counteract this limitation and improve the modeling of long-term dynamics, and more importantly, address high-dimensional recursive forecasting, this paper uses a Wasserstein GAN equipped with a progressive Lipschitz penalty and an adaptive kernel. This model is capable of taking a window of the data stream and forecasting the next values, subsequently reconstructing the time-series stream and dynamically adapting its kernel to each new window. The proposed model is a deep learning framework based on a Wasserstein GAN (WGAN-CLP) with an adaptive kernel to model alterations in streaming voltage time series. To establish the methodological foundation, we review the WGAN-LP formulation another variant model in this class and extend its framework through an adaptive kernel critic model. We then evaluate this extended model using power ratios, correlation coefficient (CC), and relative root mean squared error (RRMSE). The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms benchmark methods in both accuracy and robustness. The evaluation shows promising performance of the WGAN-CLP with an adaptive kernel framework in forecasting sequence alterations across the voltage and energy time-series datasets.

title: MPASCNet: Magnitude-Phase-Aware Adaptive Spectral Compression for Compressed Music Restoration
authors: Deng, Xinlong AND Xia, Yu AND Kong, Qiuqiang AND Cao, Yin AND Jiang, Jie
abstract: Compressed music restoration aims to recover high-fidelity audio from lossy codecs such as MP3 by restoring missing spectral content and reducing coding artifacts. Recently, generative adversarial networks and band-split models have made progress in compressed music restoration. However, existing methods either operate without explicitly modeling phase or rely on predefined frequency partitions, which may limit restoration performance and the use of input-dependent frequency information. To address these issues, we propose MPASCNet, a Magnitude-Phase-Aware Adaptive Spectral Compression network. Instead of using fixed bands, MPASCNet combines magnitude and phase features to guide cross-attention, adaptively compressing full-resolution spectral features into compact tokens. These tokens are then processed by a spectro-temporal backbone to model spectral-temporal dependencies. Finally, separate decoder branches reconstruct the full-resolution magnitude and wrapped phase spectra. title: TRIG: Toward Measuring Texture Realism in Image Generation
authors: Xu, Zhiwei AND Cui, Jiali AND Lao, Zhiqiang AND Yu, Heather AND Peng, Liang
abstract: This paper studies the backbone used by metrics for evaluating the quality of generated images. Although generative models have advanced rapidly, some outputs still exhibit unrealistic texture characteristics, and these differences are difficult to measure. Widely used evaluation metrics provide limited insight into texture realism, since they often rely on a backbone trained for another objective, such as image classification or image-text alignment. Such objectives typically encourage invariance to low-level variations that carry texture, so the resulting features primarily encode semantic and global structure. As a result, texture-specific discrepancies may not be explicitly captured. We propose TRIG, a metric directed at the texture realism of generated images. Its backbone is instead the discriminator of a generative adversarial network pre-trained on a texture dataset, which provides a learned prior for the local statistics of natural textures. A plausibility head is fine-tuned to identify local texture degradations, while preserving natural defocus and sensor noise as positive cases. On the features of this backbone, we compute a standard distributional distance between a reference set of real images and a set of generated ones. We apply TRIG to several generative models and observe closer agreement with human realness ratings than baseline metrics.

title: The Domain Is a Residue: Adapting Self-Supervised Features, Not Generators
authors: Deixelberger, Thomas AND Steinberger, Markus
abstract: Clearing fog, rain or snow from footage, or turning renders into photographs, must remove the source domain and keep the scene. Unpaired translators carry it through because their generator sees the source appearance (pixels, a near-invertible latent or a control map) and keeps it. A DINO feature map fixes what is in the scene and carries weather, lighting and rendering style as a residue of 13 to 14% of the feature norm. We propose the Representation Feature Adapter (RFA), a 2.9M-parameter network that moves this residue. We train only the adapter and its discriminators; the encoder and a feature-conditioned decoder, trained once for all conditions, stay frozen. Against CycleGAN-Turbo it is ahead on both metrics on fog and on KID on night, and level within noise on snow, rain and haze. On sim-to-real it leads REGEN and HyPER-GAN on both metrics. Only the RFA removes the rain while keeping the scene. The removal costs scene structure: CycleGAN-Turbo keeps more on every condition but fog. On VAE latents the identical adapter collapses to the identity, and decoders from other groups that never saw it render its output. The RFA has about 160 times fewer trainable parameters than CycleGAN-Turbo and under a fifth of its per-condition training time.
